question: What type of engine is the IAE V2500-A5?

options.a: A two-spool, axial-flow, high-bypass ratio turbo-fan engine
options.b: A single-spool, centrifugal-flow, low-bypass ratio engine
options.c: A three-spool, mixed-flow, ultra-high-bypass ratio engine

justification: According to page 7 of the manual, the IAE V2500-A5 engine is specifically described as a two-spool, axial-flow, high-bypass ratio turbo-fan power engine.

question: Which component is responsible for changing the available thrust rating of the V2500-A5 engine?

options.a: A mechanical adjustment on the fuel pump
options.b: A programming plug on the Electronic Engine Control (EEC)
options.c: The size of the exhaust common nozzle assembly

justification: Page 7 states that although all engines have the same basic configuration, a programming plug on the EEC is used to change the available thrust ratings.

question: What is the primary method used by the V2500-A5 engine to connect to the aircraft pylon?

options.a: Through a series of five mounting points along the core case
options.b: By forward and aft mounts attached to the pylon structure
options.c: Via the fan case flange and turbine exhaust case frame only

justification: The manual on page 7 specifies that the engine is attached to the pylon by FWD and AFT mounts, while the pylon connects the engine to the wing structure.

question: Which members of the Airbus Single Aisle family are NOT powered by the IAE V2500-A5 engine?
justification: Page 7 of the document explicitly states that the V2500-A5 can power all aircraft types of the Single Aisle family except the A318.

question: What defines the 'SELECT ONE' technology package mentioned in the engine characteristics?

options.a: A system allowing the pilot to select thrust ratings from the cockpit
options.b: Increased cooling air on 2nd stage HPT vanes and new EEC hardware
options.c: Integration of an additional stage in the Low Pressure Compressor

justification: Page 54 mentions that SELECT ONE Technology includes increased cooling air on second stage HPT vane, new second stage HPT seal and new EEC hardware.

question: A technician needs to replace an EEC on a V2527-A5 engine. To ensure the engine provides the correct 27,000 lbs thrust after installation, what must be verified?

options.a: The fuel pump flow adjuster is set to 'high flow'
options.b: The correct engine data-programming plug is installed on the EEC
options.c: A manual EEC calibration test is performed via the MCDU

justification: As per pages 7 and 54, the engine data-programming plug sets the aircraft version and thrust rating ranging from 22,000 lbs to 33,000 lbs. Without the correct plug, the EEC will not command the intended thrust rating.

question: During a thrust rating assessment for an A321, which engine versions are applicable according to the manual?
justification: Page 56 of the manual specifies that for the A321, thrust levels are achieved with the V2530-A5 (31,400 lbs) and V2533-A5 (33,000 lbs) versions.

question: If an engine is moved from an A319 to an A320, how is the take-off thrust rating increased from 24,000 lbs to 27,000 lbs?

options.a: By changing the Engine Data Programming Plug on the Electronic Engine Control
options.b: By replacing the Fuel Metering Unit (FMU) with a higher capacity model
options.c: By adjusting the mechanical stops on the Throttle Control Unit (TCU)

justification: Page 54 and 55 illustrate that the thrust rating (e.g., 24,000 lbs for A319 vs 27,000 lbs for A320) is determined by the engine data-programming plug.

question: What is the Powerplant weight of the V2500 engine as installed on the A320?
justification: The table on page 57 'ENGINE PARAMETERS' lists the Powerplant weight for the A320 version as 7500 lb or 3402 kg.

question: What is the approximate bypass ratio for the V2500 engine installed on an A319?
justification: The table on page 57 lists the Bypass ratio for the A319 version as 4.9.

question: Where is the Electronic Engine Control (EEC) located on the engine?

options.a: On the left hand (LH) side of the gearbox
options.b: On the right hand (RH) side of the fan case
options.c: Inside the core compartment near the combustion section

justification: Page 12 states: 'The EEC is on the RH side of the fan case.' This is further illustrated on page 13.

question: The FADEC alternator (Permanent Magnet Alternator) is located on the:
justification: Page 12 states: 'The FADEC alternator is on the gearbox.' This is also shown in the diagram on page 13.

question: What is the location of the two ignition boxes (exciters)?

options.a: On the LH side of the fan case
options.b: On the RH side of the engine core
options.c: Mounted directly on the main gearbox

justification: Page 14 states: 'Two ignition boxes are on the RH side of the engine core.' This is confirmed by the illustration on page 15.

question: Where is the air starter motor located on the V2500 engine?

options.a: On the RH side of the gearbox front face
options.b: On the LH side of the engine core
options.c: At the 12 o'clock position on the fan case

justification: Page 14 states: 'The air starter is on the RH side of the gearbox front face.' This is illustrated on page 15.

question: The primary fuel system components, such as the fuel pump and Fuel Metering Unit (FMU), are located on the:

options.a: Right hand (RH) side of the engine
options.b: Left hand (LH) side of the engine

justification: Page 16 states: 'The primary components of the fuel system are on the LH side of the engine. The fuel pump and the FMU are on the gearbox.'

question: To access the fuel filter for maintenance, where should the technician look?

options.a: On the LH side of the fan case
options.c: Mounted to the forward pylon bulkhead

justification: Page 16 states: 'The filter is on the LH side of the fan case.' This is shown in the detailed photos on page 17.

question: A technician needs to troubleshoot the Hydraulic Control Unit (HCU) of the thrust reverser system. Where is this unit located?

options.a: On the forward part of the pylon
options.b: On the forward part of the RH 'C' duct
options.c: On the LH side of the accessory gearbox

justification: Page 22 states: 'The HCU is installed on the forward part of the RH "C" duct.' Page 23 provides photographic confirmation.

question: The hydraulic shut-off valve for the thrust reverser system is located on the:

options.b: Aft part of the engine core

justification: Page 22 states: 'The hydraulic shut-off valve is on the forward part of the pylon.' This is critical for isolating hydraulic supply to the HCU.

question: Where are the oil scavenge pumps located on the V2500 engine?

options.a: On the fan case upper flange

justification: Page 20 states: 'The oil tank, the pressure pump, the scavenge pumps and the filter are on the gearbox.' Page 21 provides the visual location.

question: The N2 speed sensor is physically integrated into which component?
justification: Page 296 states: 'The N2 speed signal is sensed by the dedicated alternator, installed at the front face of the accessory gearbox.' The PMA provides N2 speed to the EEC.

question: What is the purpose of the Power Plant drain system?

options.a: To collect and discharge fluids leaking from the pylon and engine accessories overboard
options.b: To recycle excess fuel back into the wing tanks during shutdown
options.c: To vent internal gearbox pressure to the atmosphere

justification: Page 24 states that the system collects fluids (fuel, oil, hydraulic, water) from the pylon, accessories, and drives, and discharges them overboard through pylon and engine drains.

question: Where are fluids from the power plant system eventually discharged?

options.a: Into the combustion chamber for disposal
options.b: Through the pylon drains and the engine drains (drain mast)
options.c: Directly into the fan air stream via the 'C' ducts

justification: According to page 24 and 25, fluids are discharged overboard through pylon drains and engine drains (identified as the engine drain mast).

question: How is the engine pylon internally organized regarding leakage management?

options.a: It is a single large void where fluids pool at the bottom
options.b: It is divided into 7 compartments with various systems routed through them
options.c: It uses a vacuum suction system to pull leaks toward the rear

justification: Page 26 states: 'The engine pylon is divided into 7 compartments; various systems are routed through these areas. Any leakage... is drained overboard through separate lines in the rear of the pylon.'

question: Which system leakages are specifically routed through Zone A (Forward Fairing) of the pylon?
justification: The table on page 27 identifies Zone A as containing Flammable Fluids (fuel, hydraulics).

question: Fuel drains from core engine accessories are routed through a separate line that passes through the:
justification: Page 28 states: 'The fuel drains from the core engine accessories, are routed through a separate drain line which passes through the bifurcation panel.'

question: During a line inspection, a fluid leak is observed from the engine drain mast. What is the first recommended action according to the manual?

options.a: Immediately ground the aircraft and replace the leaking component
options.b: Run the engine at idle for 5 minutes to see if the leak stops
options.c: Check the oil quantity transmitter for a signal error

justification: Page 410 states: 'If fluid leaks are found during transit operations, run the engine at idle for 5 minutes. If the leak stops, the aircraft may be dispatched without maintenance action.'

question: If an engine drain leak persists after 5 minutes of idling, what is the limitation for dispatch if the first leakage limit is exceeded but not the second?
justification: Page 410 states: 'If the first limit is exceeded, the aircraft may be dispatched and can continue to operate for a maximum of 25 hours or 10 flights as long as the second limit is not exceeded.'

question: What is the maximum allowable leakage rate for the Fuel Metering Unit (FMU) during the second (final) limit?
justification: The chart on page 411 shows the FMU leakage limits as 0 drops/minute (Limit 1) and 40 drops/minute (Limit 2).

question: For a Hydraulic Pump leak, what is the maximum permitted leakage rate for the first limit?
justification: The chart on page 411 shows the Hydraulic pump leakage limit 1 as 3 drops/minute and limit 2 as 40 drops/minute.

question: Which of these components has its own independent drain routed to the drain mast?
justification: Page 28 states: 'Fluid drained from the oil tank scupper, fuel diverter valve and gear box mounted accessories, is independently routed to the drain mast.'

question: Where is the air intake cowl bolted onto the engine?

options.a: The rear turbine exhaust case flange
options.b: The front of the fan case flange

justification: Page 30 states: 'The air intake cowl is bolted onto the front of the fan case flange.'

question: Which system is NOT mentioned as being included in the air intake cowl?
justification: Page 30 lists the components of the intake cowl: anti-ice system, interphone jack, and P2/T2 probe. The TR HCU is on the RH 'C' duct (page 22).

question: How many identical attach fittings are used to secure the inlet cowl to the engine?
justification: Page 30 states: 'For removal and installation... the inlet cowl [has] 36 identical attach fittings.'

question: What is the weight of the V2500 Air Intake Cowl?
justification: The diagram on page 31 labels the intake cowl weight as 108 kg (238 lbs).

question: What is the construction material of the inner barrel in the air intake cowl used for acoustic purposes?
justification: Page 36 states: 'The inner barrel in the air intake cowl is made of carbon fiber composite/Nomex honeycomb for acoustic purpose.'

question: Before removing the air inlet cowl, which component must be disconnected as per the maintenance manual?

options.a: The P2/T2 sensor pressure tube and electrical connectors
options.c: The Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) oil lines

justification: Page 384 states: '...disconnect the pressure tube and electrical connectors of the P2/T2 sensor and remove the coupling at the anti-ice duct connection. Move the air inlet cowl FWD to disengage it.'

question: When installing the air intake cowl, what must the technician ensure regarding alignment?

options.a: The V-groove latch is in position number 3
options.b: The inlet cowl locating pins engage correctly to the front engine flange
options.c: The 4 alignment dowels are removed before tightening the 36 bolts

justification: Page 384 states: 'During the installation take care that the inlet cowl locating pins engage correctly to the front engine flange.'

question: How many hoisting points are provided on the inlet cowl for removal?
justification: Page 30 states that for removal and installation, there are 4 hoisting points.

question: What protection must be taken before using a work mat on the air intake cowl surface?

options.a: Coat the surface with anti-seize material
options.b: Seal the edges of the work mat with tape

justification: Page 386 advises: 'Seal the edges of the work mat with tape before you use it' to prevent tools or unwanted materials from falling into the surface/engine.

question: Which safety warning is associated with the cleaning fluid used on the air intake cowl?

options.a: It is flammable and must not be used near the ACOC
options.b: The fluid is poisonous and must be used only in an area open to the air
options.c: It causes immediate degradation of carbon fiber if not rinsed within 1 minute

justification: Page 384 gives a specific warning: 'THE CLEANING FLUID IS POISONOUS... USE ONLY IN AN AREA OPEN TO THE AIR.'

question: How many hinges hold each fan cowl door to the pylon?
justification: Page 32 states: 'Four hinges hold each door at the pylon.'

question: What is the weight of an individual LH fan cowl door?
justification: The diagram on page 33 specifies the LH door weight as 36 kg (79 lbs) and the RH door weight as 39 kg (86 lbs).

question: How many hold-open struts are installed on each fan cowl door to keep them open?
justification: Page 32 states: 'Each door is installed with... 2 hold-open struts, to open.'

question: Where are aerodynamic strakes normally installed on an A320 nacelle?

options.a: On the inboard side of the nacelle
options.c: On the rear edge of the 'C' ducts

justification: Page 32 states: 'NOTE: Note that aerodynamic strakes are installed on the inboard nacelle side (A320).'

question: How are the fan cowl door assemblies latched along the bottom centerline?
justification: Page 32 states: 'Four latches latch the door assembly along the bottom centerline.'

question: What is the maximum wind speed limit for attempting to open the fan cowl doors?
justification: Page 363 states: 'CAUTION: Caution: Do not attempt to open the fan Cowl doors if the wind speed is higher than 96 Km/h (60MPH).'

question: When opening the fan cowl doors, in what order should the four latches be released?

options.a: Starting from the rear to the front
options.b: Starting from the front to the rear
options.c: The two center latches first, then outer ones

justification: Page 363 states: 'Release the four latches starting from the front to the rear.'

question: What indication shows that a fan cowl door hold-open rod is not in the locked position during extension?

options.b: A red flag appears near the lock arm
options.c: An amber light on the pylon illuminates

justification: Page 363 states: 'The word UNLOCKED can be seen when the release collar is not in the locked position.'

question: During fan cowl door installation, what is the importance of the hinge bolts?

options.a: They must be torqued to 450 PSI before the sling is removed
options.b: They must be installed in the same positions noted during removal
options.c: They must be discarded and replaced with new ones every time

justification: Page 376 states: 'Make sure that the bolts are installed in the same positions noted during removal.'

question: If you are opening fan cowl doors in winds between 30 mph and 60 mph, what is the primary safety concern?

options.a: The wind may cause the latches to jam in the 'locked' state
options.b: The wind could move the doors causing injury or engine damage
options.c: The hold-open struts may lose hydraulic pressure

justification: Page 363 warns: 'BE CAREFUL IF YOU OPEN THE FAN COWL DOORS IF THE WIND SPEED IS MORE THAN 30 MPH (48 KM/H), INJURY OR DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR IF THE WIND MOVES THE FAN COWL DOORS.'

question: How many quick-access center latches are on the thrust reverser 'C' ducts?
justification: Page 34 states that the latch assembly includes '3 center latches, with access through a hinged access panel.'

question: What is the weight of a single LH thrust reverser 'C' duct?
justification: Page 35 and 378 state that the thrust reverser "C" duct weighs 580 lbs (263 kg).

question: What components are installed within the thrust reverser 'C' ducts to redirect airflow?

options.a: Cascades, blocker doors, and translating sleeves
options.b: Inlet guide vanes and variable stator vanes
options.c: Vectored nozzle assemblies and exhaust cones

justification: Page 34 states: 'The thrust reverser "C" ducts are in two halves installed with cascades, blocker doors and translating sleeves.'

question: How are the thrust reverser cowl doors opened during maintenance?

options.a: By using the aircraft's internal hydraulic green system
options.b: Using a hydraulic hand pump connected to an opening actuator
options.c: Manually lifting the door after disengaging the pneumatic lock

justification: Page 365 states: 'The thrust reverser cowl doors are opened using a hydraulic hand pump.' It also specifies connecting the pump to the quick-disconnect on the thrust reverser half.

question: How many attachment points for handling are found on each 'C' duct half?
justification: Page 34 states: 'Each half is installed with: - 3 attachment points for handling.'

question: What is the correct sequence for releasing the five latches on the thrust reverser 'C' duct?
justification: Page 365 lists the order as: '3 - 2 - 5 and then 6 - 4 - 1.' Latch 3 is the middle bifurcation, 2 is forward, etc.

question: A technician is opening the inboard thrust reverser 'C' duct. What aircraft configuration must be checked to avoid damage?

options.a: The landing gear must be retracted
options.b: The wing leading edge slats must be retracted
options.c: The fuel pumps must be switched to 'auto'

justification: Page 363 and 378 specify: 'CAUTION: Do not open the inboard thrust reverser "C" duct if the wing leading edge slats are extended. Damage to the thrust reverser, wing leading edge slats and wing can occur.'

question: During thrust reverser cowl door closing, how long should the system be drained after the door is closed before disconnecting the hand pump?
justification: Page 367 states: 'CAUTION: Do not disconnect the hand pump until the opening actuator system has been drained for a minimum of one minute after closing of the thrust reverser cowl.'

question: What indication appears when the V-groove latch in position number 1 is released correctly?

options.a: A green 'SAFE' light on the HCU
options.b: A red flag of the hold-open device appears

justification: Page 365 states: '...release the V-groove latch in position number 1, which will make the red flag of the hold open device appear.'

question: What tool is used to release the fan cowl doors from the hold-open device as part of the closing procedure?
justification: Page 369 states: 'Use a Phillips screwdriver to push the pin towards the door locator until the fan cowl doors are released.'

question: How many bearing compartments are identified in the V2500 engine?
justification: Page 58 states the compartments are: No. 1, 2 and 3 (front) compartment, No. 4 bearing compartment, and No. 5 which is located on the exhaust case.

question: Where is the No. 5 bearing located?
justification: Page 58 states: '...the No 5 is located on the exhaust case.'

question: Which bearing carries the axial loads generated by the LP rotor system?
justification: Page 58 states: 'The No. 1 ball bearing carries the axial loads generated by the LP rotor system.'

question: What type of load does the No. 2 bearing carry?

options.a: Axial loads of the HP rotor
options.b: Radial loads generated by the front part of the LP rotor system
options.c: Side loads from the accessory gearbox drive shaft

justification: Page 58 states: 'The No. 2 roller bearing carries the radial loads generated by the front part of the LP rotor system.'

question: The No. 3 ball bearing is responsible for carrying which loads?

options.a: Radial loads of the LPT shaft
options.b: Axial loads generated by the HP rotor system
options.c: Combined thrust of both LP and HP systems

justification: Page 58 states: 'The No. 3 ball bearing carries the axial loads generated by the HP rotor system.'

question: In which engine module is the No. 4 bearing compartment integrated?
justification: Page 58 states: 'The No. 4 bearing compartment is part of the diffuser/combustor module.'

question: How is the No. 5 bearing inner race secured to the shaft?

options.a: By an interference fit and a coupling nut
options.b: By a keyway and locking wire
options.c: By three specific curvic coupling bolts

justification: Page 58 states: 'The No. 5 bearing inner race is secured on the shaft by an interference fit and is secured against the seal assembly by a coupling nut.'

question: What is a characteristic of the No. 1 ball bearing race configuration?

options.a: It has a solid single-piece inner race
options.b: It is a split inner race ball bearing
options.c: It uses a tapered outer race for high speed

justification: Page 58 states: 'This bearing [No. 1] is a split inner race ball bearing.'

question: Which bearings are located in the LPC intermediate case module?
justification: Page 58 clarifies that the No. 1, 2 and 3 bearing compartment is built into the [intermediate] case module.

question: The Low Pressure Turbine (LPT) shaft is supported at its rear end by which specific bearing?
justification: Page 58 states: 'The Low Pressure Turbine (LPT) shaft is supported at the rear end by the No. 5 roller bearing...'

question: What is the primary function of the firewalls and fire seals?

options.a: To reduce engine noise levels during takeoff
options.b: To isolate the space in the engine into compartments and limit fire propagation
options.c: To prevent air leakage into the oil tank

justification: Page 36 states: 'The firewalls and fire seals protect from fire... isolate the space in the engine into compartments. This means isolation limits propagation, if a fire occurs.'

question: Where are the stage 2 HPT air seals located?

options.a: Between the stage 1 and 2 turbine rotor assemblies
options.b: At the front of the fan disk
options.c: Inside the No. 4 bearing scavenge valve

justification: Page 60 states: 'The stage 2 HPT air seal is located between the stage 1 and 2 turbine rotor assemblies.'

question: How is oil compartment sealing maintained to prevent oil from leaving the compartment?

options.a: By using a mechanical vacuum pump in the vent line
options.b: By using pressurized buffer air that is higher than the compartment pressure
options.c: By using magnetic seals that attract metallic particles

justification: Page 62 states: 'Oil Compartment sealing is achieved by using pressurized air, also called buffer air... buffer air pressure is higher than the pressure in the bearing compartment.'

question: Which components prevent the leakage of HPC discharge air into the diffuser case?

options.b: A double seal including a brush and knife edge seals

justification: Page 60 states: 'A double seal including a brush and knife edge seals... prevent leakage of HPC discharge air into the diffuser case.'

question: The bearing No. 5 compartment is sealed from the LPT cavity air by:

options.c: A continuous ring of VSV actuators

justification: Page 60 states: 'The bearing No. 5 compartment is sealed from the LPT cavity air by two element radial carbon seals.'

question: What modification was made to the stage 2 HPT air seals on IAE V2500-A5 engines?

options.a: The seal was changed to a brush-type to reduce friction
options.b: Modification to increase cooling air and reduce leakage on the 2nd stage vane
options.c: The seal was integrated into the LVDT for better feedback

justification: Page 60 mentions: 'In order to avoid HPT air seal cracking, a modification is made to increase cooling air and to reduce leakage on the 2nd stage vane for IAE V2500-A5 engines.'

question: Which of these is NOT a component of the front bearing compartment sealing system?

options.a: No.1 bearing front carbon oil seal
options.b: Hydraulic seal assembly for center seal
options.c: LPT stage 7 segments with braze in honeycombs

justification: Page 60 lists the components for front bearing compartment sealing: No. 1 front carbon oil seal, hydraulic seal assembly, rear brush air seal, and No. 3 rear carbon oil seal. LPT honeycombs are part of the turbine section (LPT seals).

question: Where does the air/oil mixture from the bearing compartments go after the sealing process?

options.a: It is vented directly overboard through the drain mast
options.b: It goes back into the oil system by the scavenge pump system
options.c: It is ducted to the P3/T3 sensor for air quality monitoring

justification: Page 62 states: 'The air / oil mixture goes back into the oil system by the scavenge pump system.'

question: What is the secondary role of the stage 2 HPT air seal besides sealing?

options.a: It acts as a spacer for proper axial positioning of both rotors
options.b: It provides a mounting point for the EGT thermocouples
options.c: It serves as a backup for the No. 4 bearing support

justification: Page 60 states: 'The stage 2 air seal also acts as a spacer for proper axial positioning of both rotors.'

question: Where are the separated seal segments with braze-in honeycombs installed?

options.c: Inside the diffuser case inner wall

justification: Page 60 states: 'The outer static stages 3, 4, 5 and 7 rotor seals are separated seal segments with braze in honeycombs installed in the LPT case.'

question: How many blades are on the LPC (fan) module disk?
justification: Page 64 states: 'The LPC (fan) module is a rotor assembly, which includes twenty-two blades and a disk.'

question: How many stages are in the booster section of the V2500 engine?
justification: Page 64 states: 'The LPC intermediate case module includes a four stages axial flow booster section...'

question: Where is the majority of the air ingested into the fan delivered to?

options.b: The fan discharge duct (to provide engine thrust)

justification: Page 64 states: 'A large proportion of the compressed air is delivered through the fan discharge duct to the exhaust nozzle to supply the majority of engine thrust.'

question: How many stages are in the High Pressure Compressor (HPC)?
justification: Page 64 states: 'The HPC is a ten stages axial flow module.'

question: What is the purpose of the modulated LPC bleed valve system?

options.a: To provide high pressure air for wing anti-ice
options.b: To ensure the booster has an adequate surge margin
options.c: To increase the rotation speed of the N2 shaft during takeoff

justification: Page 66 states: 'The modulated bleed makes sure that the booster has an adequate surge margin under all operating conditions.'

question: What is defined as 'Stall' in the manual's description of compressor operation?

options.a: A local effect where the airflow is not compressed
options.b: A complete reversal of airflow through the engine
options.c: The engine shutting down due to lack of fuel

justification: Page 66 defines stall as: 'Stall is a local effect where the airflow is not compressed. Stall effects can bring the compressor to surge.'

question: According to the compressor stage numbering, which stages represent the High Pressure Compressor (HPC)?
justification: Page 78 states: 'Stages 3 to 12: HP compressor.'

question: What component makes the outer annulus of the cold stream duct?

options.b: The fan case section of the LPC/intermediate case module
options.c: The inner wall of the intake cowl

justification: Page 64 states: 'The fan case section of LPC/intermediate case module makes the outer annulus of the cold stream duct.'

question: Where is the air from the booster section delivered next?

options.b: To the HPC at a suitable pressure
options.c: Overboard through the handling bleed valves

justification: Page 66 states: 'Then the air is delivered at a suitable pressure to the HPC. Then the HPC accepts air from the LPC and booster system...'

question: What is the physical effect described as 'Surge' in the manual?

options.a: The airflow expanding in a counter direction through the entire compressor
options.b: A sudden increase in fuel flow to the combustion chamber
options.c: Excessive speed of the N1 fan rotor

justification: Page 66/67 context: 'Due to the compression ratio... the airflow tries to expand in counter direction. If the entire compressor is not capable to compress the airflow... effects can bring the compressor to surge.'

question: How many fuel injectors are installed in the diffuser case of the V2500 engine?
justification: Page 68 states: 'The diffuser case has twenty mounting pads, where the fuel injectors are installed...'

question: What type of combustor is used in the V2500-A5?
justification: Page 68 states: 'The combustor is an annular type combustor...'

question: What is the purpose of the diametral difference (larger at the rear) of the diffuser section?

options.a: To increase the air speed for better ignition
options.b: To decrease air speed and change the energy of speed into pressure
options.c: To allow for thermal expansion of the HP compressor shaft

justification: Page 68 states: 'This diametral difference decreases the speed of the air and changes the energy of the speed into pressure.'

question: Which of these is NOT listed as a primary function of the combustion section?

options.a: Straighten the flow of air from the HPC
options.b: Hold the No. 4 bearing in position

justification: Page 70 lists four primary functions: straighten air flow from HPC, change air characteristics for best speed/pressure, mix fuel/air and provide ignition, and hold No. 4 bearing in position. BSBV control is an EEC function (page 249).

question: Air that surrounds the combustor is used for:

options.a: Dilution, exit temperature profile control, and cooling the combustor walls

justification: Page 70 states: 'Air, which surrounds the combustor, is used in the combustion process for dilution and in exit temperature profile control... and for the cooling of the combustor walls.'

question: Where are the igniter plugs installed on the engine?

options.a: On two mounting pads on the diffuser case
options.b: At the 12 o'clock and 6 o'clock positions of the fan case
options.c: Inside the HPT stage 1 nozzle guide vanes

justification: Page 68 states: '...two mounting pads where the igniter plugs are installed... around the [diffuser] case.'

question: How many borescope bosses are located around the diffuser case for inspection?
justification: Page 68 states: '...and six borescope bosses located around the [diffuser] case.'

question: Which bearing is physically supported by the diffuser/combustor module?
justification: Page 68 and 70 state that the No. 4 bearing compartment is part of the module and that the section functions to hold the No. 4 bearing in position.

question: What is the construction of the combustor liner?

options.a: A single piece of solid titanium
options.b: Includes an outer liner assembly and an inner liner assembly
options.c: Graphite composite outer skin with aluminum inner

justification: Page 68 states: 'The combustor... includes an outer liner assembly and an inner liner assembly.'

question: During a borescope inspection, which port would typically be used to inspect the HP turbine first stage vanes?
justification: Page 390 states: 'Here the operator is inspecting the HP turbine first stage vanes through an igniter port...'

question: How many stages are in the High Pressure Turbine (HPT)?
justification: Page 72 states: 'The HPT is a two stages turbine...'

question: How many stages make up the Low Pressure Turbine (LPT)?
justification: Page 72 states: 'The LPT is a five stages module...'

question: Which rotor system does the HPT drive?

question: If the engine oil pressure drops below 60 PSI, what happens on the ECAM?

options.b: It is directed to an air/oil rotating separator

options.c: IDG oil cooler and overboard drain mast

justification: The air/oil rotating separator directs air out of the engine via the center vent tube, rear extension duct, and flame arrestor (page 11).

question: What is the function of the cavity between the two labyrinth seals?

options.a: To collect any oil that crosses the seal and route it to drain pipes
options.b: To provide high-pressure air for the turbine clearance control
options.c: To house the magnetic chip detector probes

justification: The manual states any oil that might cross the oil seal is collected in a cavity between the seals and routed to drain pipes (page 11).

question: What is the configuration of the High Pressure Compressor (HPC) rotor in the CFM56-5B?
justification: The HPC compressor rotor is identified as a 9-stage axial flow assembly (page 13).

question: Which module supports the transfer and accessory gearboxes and contains the forward mount?
justification: The fan frame module carries inlet cowl loads, supports the gearboxes, and contains the forward mount (page 13).

question: What is the purpose of the Outlet Guide Vanes (OGVs) located before the combustion chamber?

options.a: To increase air velocity for combustion
options.b: To redirect the airflow before it enters the chamber
options.c: To filter debris from the primary flow

justification: Before entering the combustion chamber, the last stator vanes (OGVs) must redirect the airflow (page 15).

question: How many stages of the 9 HPC stator stages are variable?

options.a: The IGVs and the first 3 stages

justification: The manual states the IGVs and the stator vanes of the following 3 stages are variable (VSVs) (page 13).

question: Which systems are used to optimize the stall margin and prevent compressor surge?

options.a: The EGT probes and fuel flow transmitter
options.b: The VSVs and variable bleed valves
options.c: The chip detectors and oil relief valve

justification: To prevent compressor surge, stall effects are controlled using Variable Stator Vanes (VSVs) and variable bleed valves (page 15).

question: According to the manual, when is the compressor said to be surging?

options.a: When N1 exceeds the rating limit by 10%
options.b: When the compressor is incapable of compressing the airflow
options.c: When the chip detector pop-out indicator is extended

justification: The manual defines surge as the condition when the compressor is incapable of compressing the airflow (page 15).

question: How is a 'Stall' described in relation to compressor operation?

options.a: A global failure of the turbine shaft
options.b: A local effect where the airflow is not compressed
options.c: An automatic shutdown of the FADEC system

justification: Stall is defined as a local effect where the airflow is not compressed, which can bring the compressor to surge (page 15).

question: Where does the mechanical energy that the turbine provides to the compressor shaft transmit to?

options.a: The accessory gearbox through the radial shaft
options.b: The airflow via the compressor blades
options.c: The pylon through the forward mount

justification: The mechanical energy provided by the turbine to the compressor shaft is transmitted to the airflow with the compressor blades (page 15).

question: What is the natural tendency of the airflow due to the compression ratio within the engine?

options.a: To expand in a counter direction
options.b: To cool down immediately before combustion
options.c: To bypass the core through the TR ducts

justification: The manual states that due to the compression ratio, the airflow tries to expand in a counter direction (page 15).

question: What improvement was introduced by TECH INSERTION technology regarding the HPC?

options.b: Re-designed HPC rotor blades to improve efficiency
options.c: Replacement of VSVs with fixed stators

justification: TECH INSERTION technology introduces re-designed HPC rotor blades to improve HPC efficiency (page 13).

question: What is the combustor configuration of basic CFM56-5B engines?
justification: The manual specifies that basic CFM56-5B engines have a Single Annular Combustor configuration (page 17).

question: Which component is included in the combustion case to reduce sensitivity to the compressor air velocity profile?
justification: The case includes a diffuser for the reduction of combustion chamber sensitivity to the compressor air velocity profile (page 17).

question: How is the air flow divided at the combustion chamber?

options.a: Into primary and secondary bypass flow
options.b: Into flow that goes through the chamber and flow that encircles it
options.c: Into lubrication supply and scavenge flow

justification: The manual states the flow is divided into the flow that goes through the combustion chamber and the flow that encircles it (page 19).

question: What is the purpose of the air flow that encircles the combustion chamber?

options.a: To supply fuel to the nozzles
options.b: To provide film cooling to the first turbine nozzle
options.c: To drive the LP turbine rotor

justification: The flow that encircles the chamber provides film cooling to the first turbine nozzle and reduces gas temperature at the turbine inlet (page 19).

question: At what point does the combustion process finish?

options.c: After the 4th stage of the LPT

justification: The combustion process finishes before entering the HPT nozzles (page 19).

question: What happens to the velocity of HP gases as they pass through the diffuser?

options.b: The velocity decreases before entering the chamber
options.c: The velocity remains constant while pressure increases

justification: HP gases pass through the OGVs then in the diffuser decrease their velocity and enter the combustion chamber (page 19).

question: Which regulation standards are met by the modified dilution and improved cooling profile of TECH INSERTION engines?

options.b: Committee on Aviation Environmental Protection (CAEP) 6th meeting

justification: TECH INSERTION introduces modified dilution/cooling to reduce NOx emissions and meet CAEP 6th meeting requirements (page 17).

question: When does the combustion process start?

options.a: When fuel hits the diffuser walls
options.b: When the mixture encounters the burning zones
options.c: When N1 reaches 16% during manual start

justification: The manual states when the mixture encounters the burning zones, the combustion process starts (page 19).

question: Where does the flow that enters the combustion chamber go first in a Single Annular Combustor engine?

options.b: Through the dome to cool its surface
options.c: Directly into the HPT rotor blades

justification: The flow that enters the chamber goes first through the dome and cools its surface (page 19).

question: What is the benefit of the new HPT blades introduced by TECH INSERTION technology?

options.a: Lower aerodynamic loss between HPT and LPT
options.b: Elimination of the need for EGT monitoring
options.c: Reduction of the number of fuel nozzles to 10

justification: TECH INSERTION introduces new HPT blades with lower aerodynamic loss between HPT and LPT, resulting in reduced fuel burn (page 21).

question: The turbine section is formed by which two modules?
justification: The turbine section consists of the HPT module and the LPT module (page 21).

question: How many stages are in the LPT module nozzle and rotor?
justification: The LPT module consists of 4-stage nozzle and rotor (page 21).

question: What is the primary function of the turbines in the CFM56 engine?

options.a: To compress air for the combustion chamber
options.b: To provide energy for compressors and power accessories
options.c: To redirect air into the bypass duct

justification: The turbines provide energy to increase airflow pressure in compressors and power all accessories the aircraft needs (page 21).

question: What is the description of the HPT nozzle assembly?
justification: The HPT nozzle is a single-stage air-cooled assembly that mounts in the combustion case (page 21).

question: Which stages are included in the LPT nozzle assemblies of the LPT stator assembly?
justification: The LPT stator assembly consists of the LPT case and stages 2-4 nozzle assemblies (page 21).

question: To what structure is the turbine frame bolted?
justification: The turbine frame is bolted to the LPT case and supports the primary exhaust nozzle (page 21).

question: How is the HPT rotor assembly characterized?
justification: The HPT rotor is a single-stage, air-cooled, high-efficiency turbine (page 21).

question: Where is the stage 1 LPT nozzle assembly located?
justification: The manual states the HPT shroud and stage 1 LPT nozzle assembly is located inside the combustion case (page 21).

question: Which of these is a component of the LPT rotor assembly?
justification: The LPT rotor assembly is composed of LPT disks, stage 1 blade assembly, rotating air seals, and stages 2-4 (page 21).

question: How is energy transferred from the combustion gases to the turbine rotor?

options.a: The gases cool down and expand the LPT casing
options.b: The gases deliver energy to the turbine blades forcing the rotor to turn
options.c: The gases enter the accessory gearbox to drive the pumps

justification: Energy is delivered to the turbine rotor by gases from the combustion chambers which deliver energy to the blades forcing the rotor to turn (page 5).

question: Which of these accessories is NOT installed to the Accessory Gearbox using Quick Attach-Detach (QAD) connections?
justification: The manual states the IDG, EDP, and Starter are installed using QAD connections (page 23). The ECU is on the fan case (page 128).

question: Where is the hand cranking drive for the N2 shaft provided?

options.a: On the rear face of the accessory gearbox
options.b: On the front face of the accessory gearbox
options.c: Inside the cockpit on the maintenance panel

justification: A hand cranking drive for the N2 shaft is provided on the front face of the accessory gearbox (page 23).

question: What types of line replaceable seals are used for the gearbox gears?

options.c: Teflon O-rings or rubber lip seals

justification: Gears are plug-in units with line replaceable magnetic or spring-loaded carbon seals (page 23).

question: Where is the air starter located in relation to the gearbox?

options.a: On the RH side of the gearbox rear face
options.b: On the LH side of the gearbox front face

justification: The air starter is on the RH side of the gearbox rear face (page 130).

question: Where is the FADEC alternator (PMA) located?
justification: The manual states the FADEC alternator is on the gearbox (page 128).

question: What is the purpose of the handcranking drive mentioned in the maintenance practice?

options.a: To manually start the engine in case of starter failure
options.b: To permit manual rotation of the N2 shaft for inspections
options.c: To bleed the fuel pump before dispatch

justification: Hand cranking of the N2 shaft is provided for maintenance purposes such as boroscope inspections or checking for rotation (page 23).

question: Where is the lubrication unit installed?

options.b: On the right-hand side of the AGB front face
options.c: On the aft bulkhead of the pylon

justification: The lubrication unit is installed on the right-hand side of the AGB front face (page 455).

question: On which side of the accessory gearbox is the fuel pump assembly located?
justification: The fuel pump assembly is located on the accessory gearbox LH side (page 78).

question: Where are the Hydromechanical Unit (HMU) and fuel filter installed?
justification: The HMU and the filter are installed with the fuel pump (page 132).

question: To which component is the drain collector assembly attached?

options.b: The aft side of the accessory gearbox

justification: The drain collector assembly is attached to the aft side of the accessory gearbox (page 142).

question: Which aerodynamic station corresponds to the Exhaust Gas Temperature (EGT) measuring plane?
justification: The manual identifies STA 49.5 as the EGT measuring plane (page 25).

question: What does aerodynamic station STA 25 represent?
justification: Station STA 25 is the HPC inlet (page 25).

question: Which station represents the interface at the nose cowl inlet?
justification: Station STA 0 is the nose cowl inlet (page 25).

question: Where is the PS12 sensor designed to measure static pressure?
justification: The PS12 sensor measures static pressure from the fan inlet (page 412).

question: Which station is relevant for the measurement of compressor discharge temperature (T3)?
justification: The T3 sensor measures compressor discharge temperature, which is at STA 3 (pages 25, 410).

question: How are boroscope port angles measured on the CFM56 engine?

options.a: Counter-clockwise from the bottom centerline, forward looking aft
options.b: Clockwise from the top vertical centerline, aft looking forward
options.c: From the LH horizontal axis, clockwise

justification: Boroscope port angles are measured clockwise from the top vertical centerline of the engine, aft looking forward (page 27).

question: Where can the HPT blade leading edges be inspected during a boroscope task?
justification: The HPT blade leading edges can be inspected through the igniter holes (page 27).

question: How is a boroscope inspection generally realized?

options.b: With an optical tube equipped with a camera
options.c: Using infrared thermal imaging through the exhaust

justification: Boroscope inspections are realized with a rigid or flexible optical tube, generally equipped with a camera for visualization (page 27).

question: Which component sets the specific thrust rating (between 21600 lb and 33000 lb) for a CFM56-5 engine on the A320 family?
justification: Thrust depends on the aircraft version set by the engine data programming plug (page 32).

question: What is the take-off thrust value for a CFM56-5B4 engine installed on an A320?
justification: The manual states the take-off thrust is the same between the CFM56-5B4 on A320 and CFM56-5B7 on A319, with a value of 27000 lb (page 34).

question: What provides the interface between the engine and the aircraft for fluids, electrics, and mechanical forces?
justification: The pylons provide an interface between the engine and the aircraft for electrics, fluids, pneumatics, and mechanical forces (page 32).

question: What is the primary function of the engine nacelle?

options.b: To provide aerodynamic airflow around the engine and protect accessories
options.c: To transfer mechanical torque from the fan to the AGB

justification: The engine is enclosed in a nacelle which provides aerodynamic airflow and ensures protection for the accessories (page 32).

question: Which directions are NOT restrained by the engine aft mount?
justification: The aft mount restrains engine movement in all directions except forward and aft (page 162).

question: Which specific loads are carried by the engine forward mount?

options.a: Engine thrust, vertical, and side loads

justification: The forward mount carries the engine thrust, vertical, and side loads (page 160).

question: How many bolts and self-locking nuts are used to attach the forward mount to the pylon?
justification: The forward mount is attached to the pylon by four bolts and self-locking nuts (page 160).

question: What must be confirmed before removing the engine from the pylon?

options.a: The ENG MASTER control switch is ON
options.b: Slats are retracted and appropriate circuit breakers are open
options.c: The fire extinguisher bottles are discharged

justification: Before engine removal, make sure ENG MASTER is OFF, slats are retracted, and CBs are open (page 103).

question: On which engine side is the fluid disconnect panel located?
justification: Engine interfaces on the engine LH side include the fluid disconnect panel (page 105).

question: Where is the core electrical junction box located?

options.a: On the fan case upper part
options.b: In the zone of the forward mount

justification: The core electrical junction box is located in the zone of the forward mount (page 168).

question: How many elements compose the bootstrap system used for engine removal and installation?

options.a: One element installed at the pylon center
options.b: Two elements, to be installed at the front and at the rear of the pylon
options.c: Four elements, one for each trunnion

justification: The bootstrap system is composed of two elements, to be installed at the front and at the rear of the pylon (page 170).

question: How is the engine transportation stand fixed to the engine?

options.a: By sixteen LP turbine attach rings

justification: The transportation stand can be fixed to the engine by means of four trunnions: two front and two rear (page 173).

question: What is the composition of the inlet cowl inner barrel?
justification: The inlet cowl is composed of an acoustical composite inner barrel, outer barrel, and a nose lip (page 146).

question: How many identical attach fittings are provided for the inlet cowl?
justification: For removal and installation, the inlet cowl is provided with 36 identical attach fittings (page 146).

question: Where does the hot bleed air exhaust after passing through the cowl nose lip for anti-icing?

options.b: Through a flush exit duct in the outer barrel
options.c: Into the fan compartment ventilation zone

justification: The air exhausts overboard through a flush exit duct in the outer barrel (page 148).

question: Through what type of joint are longitudinal and transverse loads distributed into the fan case forward flange?
justification: Loads are distributed into the fan case forward flange through a bolted joint (page 148).

question: What is the structure of the acoustically treated inner barrel in the thrust reverser?

options.b: Aluminum perforated face sheet bonded to aluminum honeycomb core

justification: The inner barrel in the TR is acoustically treated and consists of aluminum perforated face sheet bonded to aluminum honeycomb core (page 156).

question: How many hoist points are provided on the inlet cowl for removal and installation?
justification: The inlet cowl is provided with 4 hoist points for removal and installation (page 146).

question: What is the purpose of installing special braces during engine removal?

options.a: To secure the ECU in position
options.b: To support the fan and TR cowls to allow engine change under the wing
options.c: To prevent rotation of the HP compressor

justification: Special braces are installed to support the fan and TR cowls, enabling the engine to be changed without removing the doors (page 107).

question: How is the primary nozzle attached to the LPT frame?

options.c: By a V-groove and J-ring clamp

justification: The primary nozzle is attached to the LPT frame by means of 16 bolts (page 158).

question: What is the function of the centerbody in the exhaust section?

options.a: To redirect bypass air into the primary flow
options.c: To house the T5 temperature sensor

justification: The centerbody provides engine center venting (page 158).

question: What forms the upper firewall of both the fan and core engine compartments?
justification: The pylon floor forms the upper firewall of both the fan and core compartments (page 156).

question: What is 'servo fuel' used for in the CFM56 fuel system?

options.a: Direct injection into the combustion chamber
options.b: Compressor airflow control and engine clearance control actuation

justification: Servo fuel is used for compressor airflow control system actuation and engine clearance control system actuation (page 181).

question: Which component uses fuel as a cooling medium to cool Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) oil?
justification: The manual states fuel is used for cooling for engine oil and Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) oil, specifically through the IDG oil cooler (pages 181, 198).

question: What is the sequence of components fuel passes through after the LP stage of the fuel pump?

options.a: IDG oil cooler, then HP pump, then FMV
options.b: Main oil/fuel heat exchanger, then filter, then HP stage
options.c: HMU, then nozzles, then wash filter

justification: After the LP stage, fuel is heated by the main oil/fuel heat exchanger, filtered, and then pressurized in the HP stage before entering the HMU (page 181).

question: Where does metered fuel flow after leaving the Hydromechanical Unit (HMU)?

options.a: Through the fuel flow transmitter and fuel nozzle filter
options.b: Back to the aircraft tanks through the FRV
options.c: To the servo fuel heater for actuation

justification: Metered fuel flows through the fuel flow transmitter, then through a fuel nozzle filter, then to the nozzles (page 184).

question: What is the maximum core engine speed (N2) limit set by the overspeed governor system?
justification: The overspeed governor system limits the core engine speed (N2) to a maximum of 106% (page 184).

question: Which cockpit control has priority over the ECU command for closing the High Pressure Fuel Shut-Off Valve (HPSOV)?

options.a: The A/THR P/B on the FCU
options.b: The MASTER lever in the OFF position

justification: The manual states the MASTER lever command has priority over the ECU command for HPSOV closure (page 192).

question: At what percentage of N2 does the micro-switch stroke open/close to inform the ECU that the governor system is in operation?
justification: The governor system micro-switch strokes open/close around 45% of N2 during each engine start (page 184).

question: What is the cockpit indication if there is a disagreement between control and position of the HP fuel SOV?

options.a: The N1 indicator circle turns amber
options.b: An ECAM warning is triggered and the engine FAULT light comes on
options.c: The FADEC automatically switches to Channel B

justification: In case of disagreement between control and position of the HPSOV, an ECAM warning is triggered and the engine FAULT light comes on (page 194).

question: Under what condition does the ECU order 'high' fuel flow return (1100 kg/h) to the A/C tanks via the FRV?

options.c: When the aircraft airspeed reaches 200 kts

justification: When the engine oil temperature has reached 95°C, the ECU sends an electrical opening signal to solenoid valves V1 and V2 for high return FF operation (page 212).

question: In case of an engine fire, what valve closure is confirmed when the fire pushbutton is pressed?

options.b: The Low Pressure (LP) fuel shut-off valve

justification: In case of emergency, the fire pushbutton is pressed to confirm the closure of the LP shut-off valve (page 204).

question: What component serves as the 'computer' of the FADEC system?
justification: The ECU is identified as the computer of the FADEC system (page 216).

question: Where is the ECU located on the engine?

options.a: Inside the combustion case at 6 o'clock
options.b: On the engine fan case right hand side
options.c: Attached to the pylon rear beam

justification: The ECU is located on the engine fan case right hand side (page 216).

question: When both ECU channels have the same health status, how is the selection of Active and Stand-by channel determined?

options.a: Channel A is always active on even dates
options.b: Selection alternates after every engine start
options.c: Channel B is permanently active for Engine 2

justification: When both channels have the same health status, Active and Stand-by Channel selection alternates after every engine start (page 218).

question: Which unit serves as an interface concentrator between the airframe and the corresponding ECU?
justification: The EIU is an interface concentrator that serves as the communication link between A/C systems and the FADEC system (page 220).

question: In case of a FADEC Control Alternator failure above 58% N2, what is the backup power source for the ECU?

options.b: The 28VDC power supply from the aircraft network via the EIU

justification: In case of control alternator failure, the ECU will automatically switch over the 28VDC power supply from the aircraft network, available as a back-up through the EIU (page 230).

question: What is the fail-safe position for Variable Bleed Valves (VBVs) if the ECU channel in control cannot ensure function?
justification: The manual provides the example that if function cannot be ensured, VBVs are moved to a fail-safe open position (page 218).

question: For maintenance purposes, how can FADEC power supply be restored on the ground with the engine shut down?

options.a: By setting the MASTER switch to ON
options.b: By using the FADEC GND PWR pushbutton switch on the maintenance panel (50VU)
options.c: By engaging the manual override on the starter SOV

justification: The ENGINE FADEC GrouND PoWeR P/B on the maintenance panel (50VU) permits power restoration on the ground (page 230).

question: When is the FADEC automatically de-powered on the ground by the EIU after engine shutdown?

options.c: Thirty minutes after N2 drops below 15%

justification: ECU automatic de-powering occurs five minutes after engine shutdown (M/S to OFF) to allow continued maintenance data transmission (page 230).

question: What is the consequence if the EIU electrical power is lost during engine operation?

options.a: The engine continues running on PMA power but restart is not possible
options.b: The EIU fails and engine start or restart is not possible
options.c: The ECU automatically switches to manual control mode

justification: The manual notes: 'If the EIU electrical power is lost, the EIU fails and engine start or restart is not possible' (page 228).

question: Which signal is received by both ECU channels as a hardwired input directly from the cockpit?

options.b: FADEC Reset from the Master Switch

justification: Each channel of the ECU receives a hardwired FADEC Reset signal from the Master Switch (page 225).

question: How many independent subsystems compose the engine ignition system?
justification: The ignition system is comprised of two independent subsystems (page 235).

question: Which component in the ignition system converts 115 volts AC into high-energy pulses?
justification: The ignition exciter converts 115 volts and sends high-voltage, high-energy pulses to the spark igniters (page 235).

question: During an automatic start, at what N2 speed is the ignition exciter energized?
justification: During an automatic start, one of the two ignition exciters is energized when the HP rotor reaches 16% of N2 speed (page 235).

question: In a manual start sequence, when must the MASTER control switch be set to the ON position?

options.a: Immediately after pressing the MAN START P/B

justification: In manual mode, when N2 is at least 20%, the MASTER control switch must be set to the ON position (page 246).

question: At what percentage of N2 does the ECU automatically close the starter SOV and cut off ignition?
justification: When the HP rotor has reached 50% of N2, the ECU closes the pneumatic starter SOV and cuts off ignition (page 235).

question: What is the voltage sent by the ECU to the ignition exciters?
justification: The manual contains a warning that the ECU sends 115 volts to the ignition exciters (page 235).

question: Which circuit breaker must be opened specifically for a 'dry crank' to ensure the HP fuel SOV remains closed?
justification: The manual states C/B 1KC1(2) (ENGINE HP FUEL SOV) is opened for dry crank only (page 255).

question: What is the cooling period required after 4 consecutive starter cycles of 2 minutes each?
justification: An acceptable duty cycle involves up to four times, then 15 minutes off for cooling (page 255).

question: What is the maximum duration the engine should be motored during a wet crank with the MASTER switch in ON?
justification: CAUTION: DO NOT MOTOR THE ENGINE FOR MORE THAN 15 SECONDS WITH THE MASTER CONTROL SWITCH IN THE ON POSITION during a wet crank (page 257).

question: Running engagement of the starter is prohibited when N2 is above what value?
justification: The manual states 'no running engagement of the starter when N2 is above 20%' (page 255).

question: How many total valves are used in the Variable Bleed Valve (VBV) system?
justification: The VBV system controls airflow using 12 valves (page 333).

question: Which component transmits the angular position of the VBV door to the ECU?
justification: A feedback sensor (RVDT) transmits the angular position of the door to the ECU (page 335).

question: How are the 11 variable bleed valves driven by the master bleed valve?

options.b: Through a series of flexible shafts

justification: The master bleed valve drives the 11 remaining valves through a series of flexible shafts (page 337).

question: Variable Stator Vane (VSV) angle is a function of core engine speed (N2) and what other parameter?
justification: Stator vane angle is a function of core engine speed (N2) and altitude (page 341).

question: To where does the VBV system bypass air from the primary airflow?
justification: The VBV system by-passes air from the primary airflow into the secondary airflow (page 335).

question: What is the purpose of the Transient Bleed Valve (TBV)?

options.a: To cool the ECU during ground operations
options.b: To improve HPC stall margin during starting and rapid acceleration
options.c: To bleed off excess fuel from the HMU

justification: The TBV system improves the HPC stall margin during engine starting and rapid transient acceleration (page 349).

question: Where does the TBV discharge HPC 9th stage bleed air?
justification: The TBV unloads the HPC by discharging stage 9 HPC air in the LPT cavity (page 343).

question: What air source is used by the LPT Active Clearance Control (LPTACC) for external case cooling?
justification: The LPTACC system uses fan air for external case cooling of the Low Pressure Turbine (page 343).

question: Which compressor stages provide air to the HPTACC system to heat or cool the HPT shroud structure?
justification: The HPTACC system uses stage 4 and stage 9 HPC air to heat or cool the HPT shroud support structure (page 343).

question: Where is the flush inlet scoop for ECU aerodynamic cooling located?

options.b: On the inlet cowl outer barrel
options.c: On the fan case LH side

justification: A flush inlet scoop, located on the inlet cowl outer barrel, supplies ram air to the ECU (page 351).

question: How is the predicted N1 value indicated on the cockpit N1 indicator?
justification: The predicted N1 is indicated by a blue circle on the N1 indicator (page 359).

question: Which of these is NOT a thrust limit mode displayed on the ECAM?
justification: The modes are CL, FLX/MCT, TOGA, and MREV (page 361). STALL is a fault condition, not a limit mode.

question: What is the linear relationship between Throttle Lever Angle (TLA) and Throttle Resolver Angle (TRA)?
justification: The manual states the relationship is linear and 1 degree TLA is 1.9 degrees TRA (page 225).

question: In Autothrust (A/THR) mode, what provides the N1 target to the ECU?

options.b: The Flight Management and Guidance System (FMGC)

justification: In A/THR function, the FMGC computes an N1 target and sends it to the ECU (page 365).

question: At what TLA is the MAX CLIMB detent point set?
justification: In the forward thrust area, the MAX CLIMB detent point is set to 25 deg.TLA (page 377).

question: At what value does the ECU consider a throttle resolver angle as a signal failure?

options.a: Less than -47.5 deg. TRA or greater than 98.8 deg. TRA
options.c: Between 25 and 35 deg. TRA without detent sensing

justification: The ECU considers a TRA value less than -47.5 or greater than 98.8 as resolver position signal failure (page 379).

question: What is the N1 target if the aircraft enters an Alpha Floor condition?
justification: In Alpha Floor condition, the A/THR function becomes active automatically and the N1 target is TOGA (page 371).

question: What is the active range for A/THR function when both engines are running?
justification: A/THR function is normally active when the throttle levers are set between IDLE and CLimb (including CLimb) (page 371).

question: How is the A/THR function disengaged via the throttle levers?

options.a: By pulling the reverse latching lever
options.b: By setting the levers at IDLE stop
options.c: By moving the levers into the TOGA detent

justification: The A/THR function is disengaged when the throttle levers are set at IDLE stop (page 373).

question: What is the maximum allowable discrepancy between the signals generated by the two throttle resolvers?
justification: The maximum discrepancy between the signals generated by two resolvers is 0.25 deg.TRA (page 379).

question: Which of these is considered an engine primary monitoring parameter on the ECAM EWD?
justification: Primary monitoring parameters on the EWD include N1, EGT, N2, and Fuel Flow (page 386). Oil and nacelle temp are secondary.

question: Where is the N1 speed sensor installed?

options.a: On the accessory gearbox rear face
options.b: In the fan frame strut No. 6 at 5:00 o'clock

justification: The N1 speed sensor is installed in the fan frame strut No. 6 at the 5:00 o'clock position (page 388).

question: How is the vibration indication processed for display on the ECAM SD?

options.a: As an absolute value in millimeters per second
options.b: As a ratio of actual value to maximum value multiplied by 10
options.c: As a percentage of the N1 speed

justification: The EVMU processes the ratio actual value/maxi value, which is multiplied by 10 and available for display (page 402).

question: What is the maximum fuel flow capacity of the Fuel Flow transmitter?
justification: The maximum flow across the FF transmitter (XMTR) is 6360 kg/hr (page 394).

question: How many thermocouple probes are used to sense and average engine EGT?
justification: The engine EGT is sensed and averaged by 9 thermocouple probes (page 390).

question: At what differential pressure range is the main oil filter clog indication generated?
justification: The main oil filter clog indication is generated when the oil differential pressure is between 29 psig (2 bar) and 33 psig (2.28 bar) (page 399).

question: Which sensor is used as a back-up for the N1 bearing accelerometer?

options.b: The Turbine Rear Frame (TRF) vibration sensor

justification: The TRF vibration sensor is used as back-up of the N1 bearing accelerometer (page 402).

question: When does the ECAM system display the 'Nacelle Temperature' indication?

options.a: Permanently during all phases of flight
options.c: Non-permanently, displayed in case of a too high temperature

justification: Nacelle temperature indication is non-permanently displayed on the SD only in case of a too high temperature (pages 396, 397).

question: How is a fuel filter clog indicated to the crew?

options.b: An amber 'CLOG' message associated with an ECAM message
options.c: A red pop-out indicator on the cockpit center pedestal

justification: A CLOG message appears in amber, associated with an ECAM message only when differential pressure across the fuel filter is excessive (page 404).

question: Which of these ECAM indications is only displayed during the engine start sequence?
justification: The manual states 'These indications (Ignition, Start Valve, Engine Bleed) are only displayed during the start sequence' (page 397).

question: The CFM56-5B thrust reverser system is which type?
justification: The thrust reverser system is of the aerodynamic blockage type (page 416).

question: How many pivoting blocker doors are installed around the nacelle for each engine?
justification: The system consists of 4 pivoting blocker doors (page 416).

question: When is thrust reverser operation possible?
justification: Thrust reverser operation is possible on ground only (page 416).

question: Which hydraulic system supplies the actuators for Engine No. 2?
justification: Hydraulic power is supplied by the green system for engine 1 and yellow system for engine 2 (page 420).

question: At what point in the angular travel of a pivoting door does the stow switch send a signal to the ECU?
justification: As soon as one pivoting door is at more than 1% of its angular travel, its stow switch sends a signal to the ECU (page 422).

question: According to the manual warning, what must be done before working on the engine to prevent accidental TR operation?

options.a: Open the LH fan cowl door
options.b: Deactivate the system using the HCU lever

justification: WARNING: The thrust reverser system should be deactivated using the HCU lever, before working on the system or on the engine (page 417).

question: Per the MEL, how are the pivoting doors secured if an aircraft must be dispatched with an inoperative thrust reverser?

options.a: Using a mechanical rope in the bypass duct
options.b: By installing special lockout bolts and red lock plates
options.c: By closing the pneumatic start SOV

justification: To lockout the pivoting doors, special lockout bolts and red lock plates are installed to secure them to the structure (page 482/501).

question: What is required to manually open the pivoting blocker door after unlocking the actuator?

options.b: Manually pulling on the edge of the door

justification: After releasing the latch and actuator, the blocker door is opened by manually pulling on the edge (page 491/512).

question: What must be installed when a pivoting door is manually opened to secure it in the open position?

options.a: A red lock plate on the storage bracket
options.b: A safety sleeve on the hydraulic actuator rod
options.c: A quick release pin through the door hook

justification: When the pivoting door is open, a safety sleeve must be installed to secure it in the open position (page 501/522).

question: When does the 'REV' indication on the ECAM change from amber to green?

options.a: When the TLA is set to -4.3 deg
options.b: When each pivoting door overshoots 95% of its travel
options.c: Immediately upon manual selection in the cockpit

justification: When each pivoting door overshoots 95% of its travel, the deploy switches are closed and the REV indication changes to green (page 435).

question: The CFM56-5B oil system is classified as which type?
justification: The oil system is a 'dry sump' full flow system (page 446/543).

question: How many pumps are contained within the lubrication unit housing?
justification: The lubrication unit has five positive displacement pumps: one oil supply and 4 scavenge pumps (page 455).

question: What is the purpose of the anti-siphon device in the oil system?

options.a: To increase supply pump output pressure
options.b: To prevent oil from draining by gravity from the tank into the gearbox after shutdown
options.c: To bleed air from the main oil/fuel heat exchanger

justification: The anti-siphon device prevents oil from draining by gravity into the gearbox after engine shutdown (page 448).

question: In the event of main oil filter clogging, how is lubrication maintained?

options.a: The supply pump automatically doubles its RPM
options.b: A bypass valve opens and oil flows through a backup filter
options.c: The FADEC initiates an automatic emergency shutdown

justification: If the main filter becomes clogged, a bypass valve opens and the oil flows through the backup filter (page 448).

question: Before returning to the tank, scavenged oil from the forward and aft sumps passes through what first?
justification: Scavenged oil circulates successively through the 4 scavenge screens and then the master magnetic chip detector (page 455).

question: According to the manual, for how long should the engine be shut down before starting oil servicing?
justification: The engine should be shut down for at least 5 minutes prior to oil servicing to allow residual pressure to decrease (page 72/493).

question: How is the red pop-out indicator of the Electrical Master Chip Detector (EMCD) reset?

options.a: Automatically when the ECU is reset
options.b: By removing the transparent cap and pushing the indicator with the thumb
options.c: By performing a wet motoring cycle

justification: To reset the red pop-out indicator, remove the transparent cap and push in the clogging indicator with the thumb (page 76/497).

question: To check for contamination, how is the EMCD plug removed?
justification: To check for contamination, remove the probe by pushing and turning the EMCD plug 1/4 turn counter-clockwise (page 76/497).

question: Which statement is true regarding the intermixing of approved engine oils?

options.a: Different brands of the same oil type are incompatible
options.b: Intermixing among different brands should be avoided
options.c: Only Royco Turbine Oil 500 can be mixed with Castrol 5000

justification: The manual states: 'There are no incompatibilities among same oil type. However intermixing among different brands should be avoided' (page 457/554).

question: What must be verified when re-installing the EMCD probe?

options.a: That the safety pin with streamer is removed
options.b: That the RED marks are aligned
options.c: That the bypass valve is set to NORM

justification: When re-installing the EMCD, verify that the RED marks are aligned (page 76/497).

question: How are the control channels designated in the Electronic Engine Control (EEC/ECU) of the A320 engines?
justification: The Electronic Engine Control (EEC) consists of two channels A and B. (Book 5A, p. 130 / Book 5B, p. 218)

subtopic: Engine fuel LP and HP pumps
question: On the IAE V2500 engine, where are the fuel pump and the FMU located?

options.a: On the LH side of the fan case
options.c: On the forward part of the pylon

justification: The fuel pump and the FMU are on the gearbox. (Book 5A, p. 16)

subtopic: FADEC power supply and permanent magnet alternator (PMA)
question: At what N2 speed does the dedicated Control Alternator (PMA) supply power to the ECU on a CFM56-5B?
justification: Each ECU is powered by a three-phase permanent magnet alternator when the engine N2 > 58%. (Book 5B, p. 216/230)

question: In the event of a single input signal failure to the EEC, how does the FADEC respond?

options.a: It immediately performs an automatic channel changeover
options.b: The channel in control uses inputs from the other channel via the cross channel data link
options.c: The engine is automatically shut down for fail-safe protection

justification: In case of single input signal failure, there is no channel changeover, the channel in control uses the inputs from the other channel through the cross channel data link. (Book 5A, p. 130)

question: When the Master switch is set from ON to OFF on the IAE V2500, which component is directly energized to stop fuel flow?

options.b: The Pressure Raising and Shut Off Valve (PRSOV) Torque Motor

justification: When the Master switch is set from On to OFF, an electrical signal is sent directly to the Pressure Raising and Shut Off Valve (PRSOV) Torque Motor (TM). (Book 5A, p. 107)

subtopic: Fuel flow control and N1/EPR scheduling
question: If the T2 sensor is no longer available on an IAE V2500, what is the resulting FADEC mode and limitation?

options.a: Rated N1 mode; N1 limit is computed using T3
options.b: Unrated N1 mode; N1 limitation is no longer computed
options.c: EPR mode; the system uses ADIRU TAT as a backup

justification: T2 is no longer available; the EEC reverts from the EPR mode to the unrated N1 mode. In this case the N1 limitation is no longer computed. (Book 5A, p. 285)

subtopic: High pressure fuel filter and fuel/oil heat exchanger
question: What is the function of the Fuel Cooled Oil Cooler (FCOC) in the IAE V2500 fuel system?

options.a: It uses engine oil to heat the fuel before the LP pump
options.b: It cools the engine oil using fuel as a heat sink
options.c: It uses fan air to cool the fuel before it enters the FMU

justification: The Fuel Cooled Oil Cooler (FCOC) cools the engine oil by using fuel. (Book 5A, p. 85)

question: The overspeed governor system on the CFM56-5B is designed to limit core engine speed (N2) to a maximum of:
justification: The overspeed governor system limits the core engine speed (N2) to a maximum of 106%. (Book 5B, p. 184)

subtopic: Fuel metering unit and hydromechanical unit (HMU)
question: Which component manages the fuel recirculation inside the IAE V2500 engine fuel system to maintain oil and fuel temperatures?

options.b: The Fuel Diverter and Return to tank Valve (FDRV)

justification: The two-position diverter valve works by managing the fuel recirculation inside the engine fuel system. (Book 5A, p. 115)

question: During engine start on the CFM56, when does the overspeed governor micro-switch normally stroke open/close to inform the ECU it is operational?
justification: This micro-switch strokes open/close around 45% of N2. (Book 5B, p. 184)

subtopic: Fuel system ECAM indications and warnings
question: What is the trigger for the 'CLOG' message to appear in amber on the ECAM SD Engine page?

options.a: Low fuel pressure at the HP pump inlet
options.b: High differential pressure across the fuel filter
options.c: High fuel temperature at the burner nozzles

justification: A CLOG message appears in amber... only when the differential pressure across the fuel filter is too high/excessive. (Book 5A, p. 310 / Book 5B, p. 404)

subtopic: FADEC power supply and permanent magnet alternator (PMA)
question: When N2 is below 10% on the V2500, what provides the 28V DC power supply to the EEC?

options.b: The aircraft 28V DC network via the EIU
options.c: The 115V AC ignition supply via a transformer

justification: The EEC is supplied by the A/C electrical power network when N2 is below 10%... through the Engine Interface Unit (EIU). (Book 5A, p. 145)

subtopic: Engine fuel LP and HP pumps
question: In the CFM56-5B fuel system, what is the flow of fuel from the aircraft tanks to the HMU?

options.a: LP Valve -> LP Pump -> Main Oil/Fuel Heat Exchanger -> Filter -> HP Pump -> HMU
options.b: Filter -> LP Pump -> Main Oil/Fuel Heat Exchanger -> HP Pump -> HMU
options.c: LP Pump -> Filter -> HMU -> Main Oil/Fuel Heat Exchanger -> HP Pump

justification: The fuel coming from the A/C tanks through the LP valve is driven by the LP stage... heated by the main oil/fuel heat exchanger, filtered, and then pressurized in the HP stage... before entering the HMU. (Book 5B, p. 181)

subtopic: Fuel metering unit and hydromechanical unit (HMU)
question: How does the ECU control the FMV on a CFM56-5B engine?
justification: The ECU channel A controls the FMV opening-closing via the Torque Motor. (Book 5B, p. 188)

question: If both EEC channels A and B are operational on a V2500, how many channels deliver output commands simultaneously?

options.c: Channel A is always master; B is only for crosschecking
