justification: All the EEC outputs are double, but only the channel in control supplies the engine control signals. (Book 5A, p. 130)

question: Where is the LP fuel Shut-Off Valve (SOV) controlled from?

options.a: Only from the Engine Fire Panel
options.b: Only from the Engine Start Panel
options.c: From the engine fire panel or from the engine start panel

justification: The LP fuel Shut-Off Valve (SOV) operation is controlled from the engine fire panel or from the engine start panel. (Book 5A, p. 109 / Book 5B, p. 206)

question: On the CFM56-5B, what is the default selection strategy for the 'Active Channel' when both channels have the same health status?

options.b: Selection alternates after every engine start
options.c: The selection is randomized by the EIU

justification: When both channels have the same health status, Active and Stand-by Channel selection alternates after every engine start. (Book 5B, p. 218)

subtopic: Fuel metering unit and hydromechanical unit (HMU)
question: What provides the command pressure to open the HP fuel SOV on a CFM56-5B during the start sequence?

options.b: The opening of the Fuel Metering Valve (FMV)
options.c: The EIU via a 28V DC solenoid

justification: When the FMV is opened, by the ECU, it provides a command pressure to open the HP fuel SOV. (Book 5B, p. 188)

subtopic: FADEC power supply and permanent magnet alternator (PMA)
question: What is the function of the time-delay relay in the V2500 PRSOV control circuit after engine shutdown?

options.a: To delay the closing of the LP SOV for 2 minutes
options.b: To de-energize the PRSOV latching torque motor 2 minutes after shutdown to avoid high temperature damage
options.c: To provide power to the EEC for post-flight BITE tests

justification: A time-delay relay automatically de-energizes the pressure raising and SOV latching torque motor 2 minutes after engine shutdown. This device avoids damage due to high temperature. (Book 5A, p. 92)

question: How is the overspeed governor system on the CFM56-5B categorized in terms of its relation to the FADEC?

options.b: Hydro-mechanical and independent of the ECU

justification: The overspeed governor is hydro-mechanical (flyweights) and independent of the ECU. (Book 5B, p. 184)

subtopic: Ignition exciter units location and function
question: Where are the two ignition boxes located on the IAE V2500 engine?

options.a: On the LH side of the fan case
options.b: On the RH side of the engine core

justification: Two ignition boxes are on the RH side of the engine core. (Book 5A, p. 14)

subtopic: Igniter plug types, location, and replacement limits
question: On the IAE V2500, how are the ignition exciters and igniter plugs connected?

options.a: Via a standard 28V DC wire harness
options.b: Via a coaxial shield ignition lead

justification: Each subsystem includes an ignition exciter, a coaxial shield ignition lead and an igniter plug. (Book 5A, p. 148)

question: During a normal automatic start on the CFM56, how does the FADEC select the igniters?

options.a: Both igniters A and B are used for every start
options.b: Only one igniter is used, and the selection alternates at each start
options.c: Igniter A is primary; B is only used for inflight restarts

justification: The selection of the spark igniter is a function of the ECU and at each start the igniter selection will be changed. (Book 5B, p. 240)

question: Which of the following conditions will trigger automatic continuous ignition on the IAE V2500?

options.c: Both Master Levers cycled to OFF

justification: Automatic Selection [of Continuous Ignition]: Engine Anti-ice ON, EIU has failed, Take Off, etc. (Book 5A, p. 176)

question: During a manual start on the IAE V2500, when is the ignition system energized?

options.a: When the MAN START P/B is pressed in
options.b: When the MASTER control lever is set to the ON position

justification: During a manual start... then the ignition system is energized when the MASTER control lever is set to the ON position. (Book 5A, p. 148)

subtopic: In-flight relight envelope and windmill start
question: If IGN START is re-selected with an engine running (IAE V2500), how many igniters are supplied?

options.a: Only the igniter scheduled for the next start
options.b: Both igniters together to provide continuous ignition
options.c: Ignition is inhibited if the engine is already running

justification: IF IGNition START is reselected with an engine running, the corresponding EEC supplies the 2 igniters together, to provide continuous ignition. (Book 5A, p. 177)

subtopic: Ignition power supply and circuit breakers
question: What is the voltage supply sent by the EEC and Relay Box to the ignition boxes?
justification: WARNING: THE EEC AND THE RELAY BOX SEND 115 VOLTS TO THE IGNITION BOXES. (Book 5A, p. 148 / Book 5B, p. 235)

question: In manual start mode on the CFM56, is there an automatic shutdown function for engine protection?

options.c: No, the operator must manually abort the sequence

justification: In case of malfunction, set the MASTER control switch to OFF to perform a start abort sequence. In manual starts there is no automatic shutdown function. (Book 5B, p. 246 / 267)

subtopic: Ignition exciter units location and function
question: What component allows the IAE V2500 start valve to be operated in the event of an electrical failure?
justification: To increase A/C dispatch, the start valve is equipped with a manual override. (Book 5A, p. 149)

question: If an ignition fault is detected during an automatic start on the IAE V2500, what is the FADEC's first action?

options.b: Stop the fuel supply and ignition, then perform a dry crank phase
options.c: Display a 'FAULT' message and continue the start using the healthy channel

justification: The FADEC stops the fuel supply and ignition, and automatically supplies airflow [dry crank] to the engine. (Book 5A, p. 203)

subtopic: Thrust Lever Angle (TLA) signal and FADEC interface
question: What is the angular relationship between the Throttle Lever Angle (TLA) and the Throttle Resolver Angle (TRA)?
justification: 1° of TLA corresponds to 1.9° of TRA. (Book 5A, p. 130 / Book 5B, p. 225)

subtopic: Engine rating modes (TOGA, FLX/MCT, CLB, CRU, IDLE)
question: Which ECAM page is automatically displayed when the mode selector is set to IGN/START?
justification: When IGNition START is selected the ENGINE page is called automatically. (Book 5B, p. 240)

question: Which of the following signals is concentrated and sent by the EIU to the ECU?

options.c: Bleed air demands from the ACSC

justification: The Engine Interface Unit (EIU) receives digital inputs from... the Air Conditioning System Controller (ACSC), for bleed air demands. (Book 5B, p. 227)

question: What is the 'fail-safe' position for the Variable Stator Vane (VSV) if the EEC is unable to control them?
justification: if the channel is faulty and the remaining channel in control is unable to control the Variable Stator Vane (VSV) position, the vanes are set to the fail-safe open position. (Book 5A, p. 131)

subtopic: Thrust reverse electrical and mechanical interlock
question: For a V2500 engine, at what TLA detection does the reverser Shut-Off Valve (SOV) open?
justification: when the potentiometers detect a Throttle Lever Angle (TLA) lower than -3°, the SOV opens. (Book 5A, p. 331)

subtopic: Manual thrust control in FADEC degraded mode
question: On the CFM56, if the 'Rated N1' mode is active, which parameter is used by the EEC to limit engine thrust?
justification: The EEC uses TLA, ADR and T2. T2 is used in N1 rated mode to limit the engine thrust. (Book 5A, p. 283)

subtopic: Alpha floor protection and autothrust interface
question: In an 'Alpha Floor' condition, what is the automatic EPR target set by the FMGS/FADEC?
justification: In alpha floor condition the auto thrust function becomes active automatically. The EPR target is TOGA. (Book 5A, p. 277 / Book 5B, p. 371)

subtopic: FADEC ground and flight mode differences
question: What 'aircraft on ground' signal is required by the EEC before it will command the thrust reverser to deploy?

options.c: Signal from the Weight on Wheels (WoW) relay in the EIU

justification: To command the thrust reverser, the EEC needs an 'aircraft on ground' signal supplied by the Landing Gear Control and Interface Units (LGCIUs). (Book 5A, p. 325 / Book 5B, p. 416)

question: Where is the N1 rating limit displayed on the ECAM?

options.a: As an amber line on the N1 dial
options.b: In green on the upper ECAM display near the mode indication
options.c: On the secondary engine page only

justification: This indication is displayed in green on the upper ECAM display near the thrust limit mode indication. (Book 5B, p. 363)

subtopic: Thrust Lever Angle (TLA) signal and FADEC interface
question: Which unit provides the 'artificial feel' and transmits throttle movement to the mechanical rod?

options.b: The throttle control artificial feel unit

justification: This rod drives the input lever of the throttle control artificial feel unit. (Book 5A, p. 287 / Book 5B, p. 377)

subtopic: Primary parameters: N1, EGT, FF (CFM) / EPR, EGT (IAE)
question: Which of the following is considered a primary engine parameter on the IAE V2500 EWD?
justification: The engine primary monitoring parameters displayed on the ECAM EWD are: EPR, EGT, N1, FF, N2... (Book 5A, p. 294)

subtopic: Secondary parameters: N2, oil pressure, oil temp, vibration
question: Where is the oil quantity transmitter (XMTR) located on both A320 engine types?
justification: The oil quantity XMTR is located in the oil tank. (Book 5A, p. 305 / Book 5B, p. 399)

subtopic: Engine vibration monitoring unit (VMU) and sensors
question: What is the equivalent value in IPS (Inch Per Second) for 1 unit of vibration displayed on the ECAM?
justification: 1 unit for N1 or N2 rotor corresponds to 0.3IPS (Inch Per Second). (Book 5A, p. 292)

subtopic: ECAM ENG page primary and secondary display layout
question: When is the 'Nacelle Temperature' indication displayed on the ECAM?

options.c: Displayed if it is at or above 320°C (IAE) or in case of high temperature (CFM)

justification: NACELLE TEMPERATURE INDICATION (DISPLAYED IF ONE NACELLE TEMPERATURE IS AT OR ABOVE 320°C). (Book 5A, p. 303 / Book 5B, p. 397/406)

subtopic: EGT limit zones and exceedance logic
question: What is the maximum EGT limit during the engine start sequence on a CFM56-5B?
justification: The maximum EGT during start sequence is 725º C. (Book 5B, p. 240)

subtopic: Dual engine monitoring in FADEC cross-channel data
question: In case of SDAC failure, which unit acts as a backup to send oil quantity and pressure data to the DMCs?
justification: In case of SDACs failure, the EIU sends data to DMCs by the FWCs. (Book 5A, p. 133)

subtopic: Secondary parameters: N2, oil pressure, oil temp, vibration
question: Which secondary parameters are also displayed on the ECAM CRUISE page?

options.b: Fuel used, oil quantity and vibration
options.c: Start valve position and Igniter status

justification: Fuel used, oil quantity and vibration indications are also displayed on the ECAM CRUISE page. (Book 5A, p. 302 / Book 5B, p. 396)

subtopic: Engine vibration monitoring unit (VMU) and sensors
question: What is the function of the N1 'trim balance sensor' on the IAE V2500?

options.a: It provides a backup N1 signal to the EEC
options.b: It sends N1 analog signals to the EVMU for on-board fan trim balancing
options.c: It limits N1 speed during high vibration events

justification: one sensor sends N1 analog signals (trim balance sensor) to the Engine Vibration Monitoring Unit... and is capable of on-board fan trim balancing. (Book 5A, p. 296/292)

subtopic: Primary parameters: N1, EGT, FF (CFM) / EPR, EGT (IAE)
question: How many thermocouple probes sense the engine EGT on a CFM56-5B?
justification: The engine EGT is sensed and averaged by 9 thermocouple probes located in the T49.5 plane. (Book 5B, p. 390)

question: What happens if the oil pressure drops below 60 PSI on a V2500 engine?

options.b: The ECU automatically shuts down the engine
options.c: The oil low pressure switch triggers an LOP warning and the indication becomes red

justification: The Oil LOW PRESSURE switch sends its discrete signal... when the pressure drops below 60 PSI. ... indication becomes amber [below 80] and red if the pressure drops below 60 PSI. (Book 5A, p. 357)

question: On the IAE V2500 engine, how many internal discharge ports are contained within the Fuel Distribution Valve (FDV)?
justification: The FDV receives metered fuel... then into ten internal discharge ports. (Book 5A, p. 99)

question: Where is the T12 sensor (engine intake air temperature) located on the CFM56-5B?

options.a: On the fan frame strut No. 6
options.b: On the engine fan inlet case at the 1:00 o'clock position
options.c: At the 4:30 o'clock position in the fan frame

justification: The T12 sensor... is installed on the engine fan inlet case at the 1:00 o'clock position. (Book 5B, p. 412)

question: How is the Electrical Master Chip Detector (EMCD) probe on the CFM56-5B removed from its housing?

options.a: Pulled straight out after removing a safety pin

justification: remove the probe as follows: ... push and turn the EMCD plug 1/4 turn counterclockwise. (Book 5B, p. 76)

question: In the IAE V2500 fuel system, what happens if the fuel filter becomes clogged?

options.a: The engine is automatically shut down by the EEC
options.b: A bypass valve opens in the fuel filter pressure plate to ensure continued flow
options.c: The LP pump pressure is increased to force fuel through the filter

justification: The fuel filter bypass valve makes sure that the fuel still flow in the event of fuel filter clogging. (Book 5A, p. 85/86)

question: On a CFM56-5B, if the Control Alternator (PMA) fails in flight while N2 is above 58%, what is the FADEC response?

options.a: The engine enters a mechanical backup mode
options.b: The ECU automatically switches to the 28V DC power from the aircraft network
options.c: The ECU initiates an emergency shutdown sequence

justification: In case of control alternator failure, the ECU will automatically switch over the 28VDC power supply from the aircraft network, available as a back-up through the EIU. (Book 5B, p. 230)

question: Under what condition does the IAE V2500 EEC use synthesized values for engine control?
justification: dual input signal failure, the system runs on synthesized values of the healthiest channel. (Book 5A, p. 130)

question: On the CFM56-5B, why does the ECU use the Engine Oil Temperature as its primary reference for the Fuel Return Valve (FRV) logic?

options.a: Because fuel and oil temperatures are completely independent
options.b: Because engine oil gets hot as the IDG oil gets hot due to the successive heat exchangers
options.c: Because it is the only temperature sensor available on the gearbox

justification: The ECU uses the Engine Oil Temperature as its reference because the engine oil gets hot as the IDG oil gets hot, due to the recirculation fuel is going successively through the engine and IDG oil/fuel heat exchangers. (Book 5B, p. 200)

question: In the IAE V2500 FADEC system, if Channel A fails, how does Channel B receive command signals from the EIU?

options.a: Directly from the EIU via its own ARINC 429 bus
options.b: Via a cross-channel data link from Channel A only
options.c: It does not receive signals; Channel B is strictly a monitor

justification: Each channel receives inputs for both the Air Data/Inertial Reference Units (ADIRUs) and the EIU. (Book 5A, p. 136) [Note: Unlike CFM where EIU data is only received by Chan A, V2500 EEC channels receive inputs independently].

question: During a CFM56-5B automatic start sequence, at what N2 percentage is fuel flow normally initiated?
justification: When N2 reaches 22% the ECU controls... HP fuel SOV opening. At this percentage of N2, fuel flow begins. (Book 5B, p. 240)

question: What ECAM action is triggered on the CFM56-5B if there is a disagreement between the commanded position and the actual position of the HP fuel SOV?

options.b: A warning is triggered and the engine FAULT light comes on
options.c: The opposite engine is automatically commanded to MCT

justification: In case of disagreement between control and position, an ECAM warning is triggered and the engine FAULT light comes on. (Book 5B, p. 194)

question: On the CFM56-5B, on which side of the fan compartment is the fuel pump and Hydromechanical Unit (HMU) installed?
justification: The primary components of the fuel system are installed on the LH side of the fan compartment. (Book 5B, p. 132)

question: How many fuel manifolds are used to supply the 20 nozzles on the IAE V2500 engine?
justification: The fuel flow is then routed to a fuel distribution valve, which supplies 20 nozzles through 10 manifolds. (Book 5A, p. 97)

question: In the IAE V2500 heat management system, which modes represent 'no return to tank' conditions?
justification: modes 3 and 5 are no return to tank modes. (Book 5A, p. 115)

question: What type of filter is used to deliver fuel to the HMU servo valves on a CFM56-5B?
justification: Filtered fuel is delivered, from a self-cleaning wash filter, through a servo fuel heater to the servo valves of the HMU. (Book 5B, p. 196)

question: During a wet motoring sequence on a CFM56, why must the MASTER lever be set to ON?

options.b: To permit the opening of the HP fuel SOV
options.c: To command the starter SOV to its 50% position

justification: Opening of the HP fuel SOV is also possible when the rotary selector is set to CRANK and the MASTER lever is set to ON, to permit a wet motoring. (Book 5B, p. 188)

question: If both EEC channels A and B experience a complete output signal failure on a V2500, what is the effect on the engine components?

options.a: They remain in their last commanded position
options.b: They are moved to a fail-safe position
options.c: The engine continues at the current power setting via mechanical links

justification: complete output signal failure, there is no longer any current... the related component will go to the 'fail-safe' position. (Book 5A, p. 130)

question: On the IAE V2500, what happens in Mode 3 when the engine is at a high power setting?

options.a: All heat is absorbed by the burned fuel and return to wing tank is stopped
options.b: The IDG oil is cooled by fan air through the ACOC exclusively
options.c: Fuel is returned to the tank at a rate of 1000 kg/h

justification: MODE 3: Engine at high power setting: In this condition all the heat is absorbed by the burned fuel... The fuel flow to the wing tank is stopped. (Book 5A, p. 123)

question: When validating air data for engine control on the V2500, which data source is preferred by the EEC?
justification: The EEC performs validation tests... ADIRU data is preferred over engine data. (Book 5A, p. 136)

question: On the CFM56-5B, at what oil temperature does the ECU first energize the V1 solenoid for low flow fuel recirculation?
justification: Engine oil temperature at 90°C, the ECU energizes the V1 solenoid and low flow fuel recirculation begins. (Book 5B, p. 210)

question: What are the two fuel flow return levels for the CFM56-5B Fuel Return Valve (FRV)?
justification: The two return fuel flow levels are 500 kg/h and 1000 kg/h. (Book 5B, p. 208)

question: Which component in the IAE V2500 fuel system allows for fuel flow adjustment between 'high flow' and 'normal flow' by maintenance personnel?
justification: A flow adjuster installed below the metering valve is used for the fuel flow adjustment... by a maintenance action. (Book 5A, p. 97)

question: What is the working range for analog inputs received by the IAE V2500 Engine Interface Unit (EIU)?
justification: analog inputs which are of the differential type with a working range of 1 to 9 volts. (Book 5A, p. 140)

question: What prevents oil from draining by gravity from the tank through the pump on the CFM56 after engine shutdown?

options.a: A check valve in the pump outlet
options.b: The anti-siphon device using air from the forward sump

justification: The anti-siphon device prevents oil from draining by gravity... after engine shutdown. It uses air from the forward sump. (Book 5B, p. 448)

question: How long after aircraft power-up are the CFM56 ECUs automatically supplied with aircraft power if the engines are not running?
justification: At initial A/C power-up, both engine ECUs are supplied with aircraft power for 5 minutes. (Book 5B, p. 230)

question: On the IAE V2500, what happens to the fuel remaining in the upper eight manifolds at engine shutdown?

options.a: It is sucked back to the oil tank
options.b: It is drained into the engine through the two lowest fuel manifolds
options.c: It is trapped in the manifolds by the check valves

justification: This lets remaining fuel from the upper eight fuel manifolds to be drained into the engine through the two lowest fuel manifolds. (Book 5A, p. 99)

question: Which command has priority for the closure of the CFM56 HP fuel SOV?
justification: The MASTER lever command has priority over the ECU command. (Book 5B, p. 192)

question: If the IDG oil temperature is excessive on an IAE V2500, how does the heat management system respond regarding fuel return?

options.b: Return to tank is not permissible (Mode 5 - Fail-safe)
options.c: It initiates an automatic IDG disconnect

justification: MODE 5: ... return to tank is not permissible due to the high return fuel temperature [caused by excessive IDG temp]. (Book 5A, p. 125)

question: How is the return fuel flow to the aircraft tanks modulated on the IAE V2500?

options.a: By a three-way solenoid on the EEC
options.b: By the Fuel Diverter and Return to tank Valve (FDRV) through software logic based on oil/fuel limits
options.c: By a dedicated pump in the pylon

justification: The EEC processes the operation modes of the fuel diverter and return valve by software logic... generated around the limiting temperatures of fuel and oil. (Book 5A, p. 101)

question: Which parameter on the CFM56-5B is used to determine the 'Predicted N1' circle on the ECAM?
justification: The predicted N1... corresponds to the value determined by the Throttle Lever Angle (TLA). (Book 5B, p. 359)

question: What protection is provided if the 200-micron strainer in the IAE V2500 Fuel Distribution Valve becomes blocked?

options.a: A clog signal is sent to the EEC

justification: The fuel goes through a 200-micron strainer... If the strainer gets blocked, a bypass valve will open. (Book 5A, p. 99)

question: What is the source of electrical supply for the CFM56-5B engine ignition system?
justification: The ignition is supplied by 115 VAC. (Book 5B, p. 225)

question: Where is the Fuel Cooled Oil Cooler (FCOC) installed on the IAE V2500 engine?

options.a: On the RH side of the core

justification: The Fuel Cooled Oil Cooler (FCOC)... is installed on the left fan case. (Book 5A, p. 85)

question: Which valve in the CFM56-5B HMU provides overspeed protection independently of the ECU?

options.b: The Delta P valve (through the overspeed governor)

justification: The overspeed governor is hydro-mechanical (flyweights) and independent of the ECU. The Delta P valve is hydraulically forced to cause the by-passed valve to stroke more open. (Book 5B, p. 184)

question: On the IAE V2500, how many N1 speed sensors are installed in the front bearing compartment to support the EEC channels?
justification: The fan speed (N1) indicating system has 4 sensors: o two sensors... o one sensor is a spare... (Total 3 sensors for EEC). [Note: The 4th is for VMU]. (Book 5A, p. 296)

question: When the CFM56-5B engine oil temperature reaches 95°C, what return fuel flow rate is commanded?
justification: When the engine oil temperature has reached 95°C... to allow a higher return fuel flow... 1000 kg/h. (Book 5B, p. 212)

question: Which computer acts as the primary interface concentrator between the A/C systems and the FADEC system for both engine types?

options.a: The Flight Management and Guidance Computer (FMGC)

justification: The EIU is an interface concentrator that serves as the communication link, between the A/C systems and the FADEC system. (Book 5A, p. 140 / Book 5B, p. 220)

subtopic: Fuel Diverter and Return Valve operation
question: On the IAE V2500, what is the 'fail-safe' mode of operation for the heat management system?
justification: MODE 5: ... NOTE: This is the fail-safe mode of operation. (Book 5A, p. 125)

question: On the ground, when does the CFM56 ECU automatically de-power after engine shutdown (MASTER lever to OFF)?
justification: ECU automatic de-powering on the ground... five minutes after engine shut down (M/S to OFF). (Book 5B, p. 230)

question: In the CFM56-5B Fuel Return Valve (FRV) assembly, what keeps the return fuel flow constant?
justification: The compensating valve will move to keep the return fuel flow constant. (Book 5B, p. 212)

question: On the CFM56-5B, which channel receives command signals from the EIU via the bus network?
justification: Data from the EIU, however, are received by channel A only and transmitted by the internal Cross Channel Data Link to channel B. (Book 5B, p. 225)

question: What is the weight of the IAE V2500 air starter?
justification: BE CAREFUL DURING REMOVAL OR INSTALLATION OF THE STARTER, IT WEIGHS 33 LBS (15 KG). (Book 5A, p. 392)

question: On the IAE V2500, at what N2 speed should the ground crew be told to close the start valve during a manual start?
justification: When N2 is at 43%, tell the ground crew to close the start valve. (Book 5A, p. 191)

question: What is the primary function of the ignition boxes (exciters) on the IAE V2500 engine?

options.a: To provide high-pressure air for starting
options.b: To convert 115 Volts into high voltage, high-energy pulses
options.c: To monitor the spark duration for the FADEC

justification: THE EEC AND THE RELAY BOX SEND 115 VOLTS TO THE IGNITION BOXES, WHICH CONVERT IT AND SEND HIGH ENERGY PULSES. (Book 5A, p. 148)

question: During a manual start on the CFM56-5B, which of the following will cause an automatic abort by the FADEC?

options.b: EGT overlimit or compressor stall detection
options.c: The FADEC never aborts a manual start

justification: Note that also a manual start can be automatically aborted in case of EGT overlimit or compressor stall detection. (Book 5B, p. 235)

question: What is the maximum continuous operation limit for the IAE V2500 starter during motoring?
justification: or 4 continuous minutes on, then 30 minutes off for cooling. (Book 5A, p. 183)

question: During an IAE V2500 automatic start, the EEC closes the start valve and cuts off ignition when N2 reaches:
justification: When N2 reaches 43%, the EEC closes the starter valve and cuts off the ignition. (Book 5A, p. 159)

question: If an engine stall is sensed during an IAE V2500 automatic start, what is the FADEC's immediate action?

options.a: It resets the EEC and tries again after 30 seconds
options.b: It stops fuel and ignition, performs a dry crank phase, and then aborts the sequence
options.c: It forces the engine into Mode 5 fail-safe

justification: The FADEC stops the fuel and the ignition, then a dry crank phase is automatically done. After the auto-cranking, the FADEC aborts the start sequence. (Book 5A, p. 209)

question: After three consecutive cycles of 2 minutes on / 15 seconds off, how long must the IAE V2500 starter cool down?
justification: 3 consecutive cycles; 2 minutes on, 15 seconds off up 2 times and one minute on, then 30 minutes off for cooling. (Book 5A, p. 183)

question: Which EIU logic will trigger automatic continuous ignition on the IAE V2500?

options.a: Approach idle selected by the EIU
options.c: Master lever set to ON for the second engine start

justification: Automatic Selection [of Continuous Ignition]: ... Approach idle selected by the EIU. (Book 5A, p. 176)

question: During a CFM56-5B automatic start, up to what N2 percentage is the FADEC able to abort the start sequence in case of an incident?
justification: In automatic mode the ECU is able, up to 50% N2, to abort the start sequence in case of an incident. (Book 5B, p. 238)

question: Where is the air starter located on the CFM56-5B engine?

options.a: On the RH side of the gearbox front face
options.b: On the RH side of the gearbox rear face
options.c: On the LH side of the core

justification: The air starter is on the RH side of the gearbox rear face. (Book 5B, p. 130)

question: To start a manual engine start sequence on the IAE V2500, what is the first cockpit action after selecting IGN START?

options.b: Press the ENG MAN START P/B to ON
options.c: Select CRANK on the mode selector

justification: Action on the ENG MANual START P/B opens the starter valve, via the EEC. After 30 seconds dry crank, set the ENG/MASTER control switch to ON. (Book 5A, p. 165)

question: What happens if you open the IAE V2500 starter valve manual override without the starter system being pressurized?

options.a: The engine will dry crank slowly
options.c: Damage to the valve can occur

justification: NOTE: Do not operate the valve unless the starter system is pressurized. Damage to the valve can occur. (Book 5A, p. 408)

question: In a CFM56-5B automatic start sequence, at what N2 speed does the ECU provide ignition?
justification: When N2 reaches 16% the ECU provides ignition. (Book 5B, p. 240)

question: What is the required cooling time after 4 consecutive starter cycles on a CFM56-5B?
justification: after 4 cycles, wait 15 minutes before attempting a new start. (Book 5B, p. 285)

question: If an automatic start on an IAE V2500 engine fails, why must the MASTER lever be set to OFF after the FADEC aborts the sequence?

options.b: To confirm the abort and allow the sequence to fully terminate
options.c: To manually close the LP SOV

justification: After the auto cranking, the FADEC aborts the start sequence. Then the MASTER lever must be set to OFF. (Book 5A, p. 209/234)

question: What is the time limit for motoring the IAE V2500 engine with the MASTER control switch in the ON position during a wet crank?
justification: CAUTION: - DO NOT MOTOR THE ENGINE FOR MORE THAN 15 SECONDS WITH THE MASTER CONTROL SWITCH IN THE ON POSITION. (Book 5A, p. 187)

question: During an IAE V2500 manual start, what happens immediately after the MASTER lever is set to ON?

options.a: Only ignition system A is energized
options.b: Both ignition systems are energized and LP/pressure raising SOVs open
options.c: The start valve opens automatically via EEC logic

justification: As soon as the MASTER lever is in the ON position, both ignition systems are energized, LP and pressure raising SOVs open and the fuel flow increases. (Book 5A, p. 167)

question: If engine light-up is not obtained within 15 seconds during a CFM56 automatic start, what does the FADEC do?

options.a: Immediately aborts the start and displays a FAULT message
options.b: Automatically turns fuel and ignition OFF, dry cranks for 30 seconds, then initiates a second attempt
options.c: Switches to continuous ignition and increases fuel flow

justification: If engine light-up is not obtained within 15 seconds, the FADEC automatically turns the ignition and the fuel OFF and dry cranks the engine for 30 seconds before initiating automatically a new start. (Book 5B, p. 293)

question: In the IAE V2500, what happens if the MASTER lever is cycled from ON to OFF then back to ON with the engine running?

options.b: The continuous ignition function is automatically selected
options.c: The EEC reverts to unrated N1 mode

justification: Automatic Selection [of Continuous Ignition]: ... MASTER LEVER CYCLED FROM ON TO OFF THEN BACK TO ON. (Book 5A, p. 176)

question: What tool is used to move the start valve manual handle to the OPEN position on the IAE V2500?
justification: Use a 3/8" square drive to move the start valve manual handle to the OPEN position. (Book 5A, p. 408)

question: After performing a wet crank on the IAE V2500, for how long should the engine be dry cranked to eliminate fuel vapors?
justification: After wet cranking... Continue to dry crank for at least 60 seconds. (Book 5A, p. 187)

question: Which ECAM message and light appear if the IAE V2500 start valve fails to open?

options.a: ENG 1 START VALVE FAULT message and engine FAULT light
options.b: X BLEED VALVE NOT OPEN message and engine FIRE light
options.c: STARTER PRESS LOW message and MASTER CAUTION light

justification: If the start valve does not open... The MASTER CAUTion and the ENGine FAULT lights come on. An ECAM message comes into view. (Book 5A, p. 191)

question: During the second attempt of a CFM56-5B automatic start after an ignition fault, when are both igniters re-energized?

options.b: At the 25th second of the dry crank period
options.c: At the 50th second of the dry crank period

justification: SECOND ATTEMPT: At the 25th second of the dry crank period, both ignitors are re-energized. (Book 5B, p. 295)

question: In a CFM56 manual start sequence, at what N2 speed must the MASTER control switch be set to the ON position?
justification: After that, the N2 begins to increase and, when it is at least 20% N2, the MASTER control switch must be set to the ON position. (Book 5B, p. 246)

question: When is the continuous relight function cut off on both A320 engine types?

options.b: When the mode selector is moved back to the NORM position

justification: The continuous relight is cut off in MODE NORMal. (Book 5A, p. 179 / Book 5B, p. 253/273)

question: If an EGT overlimit is detected during a CFM56-5B automatic start, how many additional attempts will the FADEC automatically perform?
justification: 4 start attempts will be done, a normal start plus 3 additional attempts. (Book 5B, p. 299)

question: If an IAE V2500 start valve fails to close at 43% N2, which procedure must be performed by the crew?

options.a: Manually close the valve via the 3/8" square drive
options.b: START VALVE NOT CLOSED procedure, including setting X BLEED to SHUT
options.c: Select MODE selector to CRANK to reset the EEC

justification: If the start valve does not close... You must perform the START VALVE NOT CLOSED procedure. For this, you must remove all bleed sources... Set the X BLEED selector to SHUT. (Book 5A, p. 199/224)

question: What is the total cumulative fuel schedule reduction applied by the FADEC by the start of the fourth attempt on a CFM56-5B?
justification: The fuel schedule reduction in the fourth start is 7 percent (a total of 21 percent). (Book 5B, p. 299)

question: In manual start mode on the CFM56, if a stall or EGT overlimit occurs, how must the crew abort the start?

options.b: Set the MASTER control switch to OFF
options.c: Cycle the ENG MODE selector to NORM

justification: In case of malfunction, set the MASTER control switch to OFF to perform a start abort sequence. In manual starts there is no automatic shutdown function. (Book 5B, p. 246)

question: How many resolvers are contained within the Throttle Control Unit (TCU) for engine control?
justification: The throttle control unit comprises: ... -2 resolvers (one resolver per FADEC channel). (Book 5A, p. 379 / Book 5B, p. 379)

question: Where are the Engine Interface Units (EIUs) located in the aircraft?
justification: Each EIU, located in the avionics bay, is an interface concentrator. (Book 5A, p. 133 / Book 5B, p. 222)

question: On the throttle control lever, which TLA corresponds to the 'Max Climb' detent point?
justification: In the forward thrust area, there are two detent points, the MAX CLIMB detent point set to 25 deg.TLA. (Book 5A, p. 377 / Book 5B, p. 377)

question: What thrust limit mode is displayed on the ECAM if the throttle levers are set at the 35 degree TLA position on the ground?
justification: the MAX CONTINUOUS/FLEX TAKE-OFF detent point set to 35 deg.TLA. ... On ground... FLEX N1 is displayed whenever the thrust lever position is between IDLE and FLX/MCT. (Book 5A, p. 377 / Book 5B, p. 361)

question: If electrical power to the EIU is lost, what is the effect on engine starting?

options.a: The engine can still be started in manual mode
options.b: Engine start or restart is not possible
options.c: The engine automatically restarts in continuous relight mode

justification: NOTE: If the EIU electrical power is lost, the EIU fails and engine start or restart is not possible. (Book 5B, p. 228)

question: How does the autothrust function behave when the aircraft enters an 'Alpha Floor' condition?

options.a: It disconnects to allow manual pilot control
options.b: It becomes active automatically and sets the N1 target to TOGA
options.c: It limits engine output to MCT to prevent overboost

justification: Note: In Alpha Floor condition the A/THR function becomes active automatically. The N1 target is TOGA. (Book 5B, p. 371)

question: When engaged, when does the A/THR function become 'active' after takeoff?

options.a: As soon as the aircraft reaches 100 feet
options.b: When the throttle levers are set to the CLimb detent
options.c: When the landing gear is retracted

justification: When engaged, the A/THR function becomes active when the throttle levers are set to CLimb detent after take off. (Book 5B, p. 371)

question: If the throttle levers are set between two detent points, which detent determines the thrust limit mode?

options.c: Neither; the system stays in the previous mode

justification: If the throttle levers are set between two detent points, the upper detent will determine the thrust limit mode. (Book 5B, p. 361)

question: Which Throttle Resolver Angle (TRA) value range is considered a position signal failure by the IAE V2500 EEC?

options.a: Less than -20.0 deg.TRA or greater than +45.0 deg.TRA
options.b: Less than -47.5 deg.TRA or greater than 98.8 deg.TRA

justification: The ECU considers a throttle resolver angle value: - less than -47.5 deg.TRA or - greater than 98.8 deg.TRA as resolver position signal failure. (Book 5A, p. 379)

question: In case of a single engine operation on the IAE V2500, what is the active range of the auto thrust function?
justification: NOTE: The auto thrust function active range is extended to MCT in the case of single engine operation. (Book 5A, p. 277)

question: What is the total angular movement range of the throttle control lever (from full reverse to full forward)?
justification: The throttle control lever moves over a range from -20 deg. TLA (Reverser Full Throttle stop) to +45 deg. TLA. (Book 5A, p. 377 / Book 5B, p. 377)

question: How many Engine Interface Units (EIUs) are installed on the aircraft for engine control?

options.c: One central unit for both engines

justification: There is one EIU for each engine. (Book 5A, p. 140 / Book 5B, p. 222)

question: If FLEX mode is selected, where must the thrust lever be positioned for FLEX N1 to be displayed on the ground?
justification: if FLEX mode is selected, FLEX N1 is displayed whenever the thrust lever position is between IDLE and FLX/MCT. (Book 5B, p. 361)

question: What is the TLA detent point for the Maximum Continuous Thrust (MCT) mode?
justification: the MAX CONTINUOUS/FLEX TAKE-OFF detent point set to 35 deg.TLA. (Book 5A, p. 377 / Book 5B, p. 377)

question: Which action on the IAE V2500 sends an electrical signal to isolate the aircraft fuel system from the engine?

options.a: Moving the TLA to full reverse
options.b: Setting the Master switch to OFF
options.c: Opening the fuel cooled oil cooler bypass

justification: When the Master switch is set... to OFF... A second electrical signal is sent to the two motors of the LP Valve, which is controlled to close. (Book 5A, p. 107)

question: What happens to the EPR indicator on the ECAM if a sensor failure causes the V2500 FADEC to revert to rated N1 mode?

options.a: It turns amber and shows the N1 target
options.c: It is replaced by a green T2 indication

justification: In case of EPR sensor failure... the EPR indicator is crossed amber. (Book 5A, p. 283)

question: At what throttle lever position is the auto thrust function automatically disengaged?
justification: The A/THR function is disengaged when the throttle levers are set at IDLE stop. (Book 5A, p. 279 / Book 5B, p. 373)

question: What is the maximum allowable discrepancy between the signals generated by the two resolvers in the Throttle Control Unit?
justification: The maximum discrepancy between the signals generated by two resolvers is 0.25 deg.TRA. (Book 5A, p. 379)

question: On an IAE V2500, if the A/THR is active and the throttle levers are set between two detent points, what limits the EPR command?
justification: When the throttle levers are set between two detent points, the EPR command is limited by the throttle lever position. (Book 5A, p. 277)

question: Which signal from the IAE V2500 EIU tells the Bleed Monitoring Computer (BMC) to close the PRV during starting?

options.b: A ground signal when the start valve moves away from the closed position
options.c: When the mode selector is moved to CRANK

justification: the EIU generates a ground signal for the BMC when the start valve moves away from the closed position. On receipt of this ground signal, the BMC closes the... PRV. (Book 5A, p. 141)

question: Which component is pulled up to override the intermediate mechanical stop at 0 deg TLA on the throttle levers?
justification: This stop is overridden when the reverse latching lever is pulled up for selection of the reverse power. (Book 5A, p. 377 / Book 5B, p. 377)

question: On the IAE V2500 ECAM, where is the 'predicted EPR' (white circle) displayed?

options.c: In the center of the EWD

justification: The predicted Engine Pressure Ratio (EPR) is indicated by a white circle on the EPR indicator. (Book 5A, p. 265)

question: What happens if the A/THR is NOT active and the throttle levers are moved between 0 and 35 degrees TLA?

options.a: The FADEC automatically engages the A/THR
options.b: The engine control is in manual mode
options.c: The engine will stay at IDLE

justification: In the middle throttle range (0deg. To 35 deg.TLA)... If the autothrust is not engaged, the engine control is manual. (Book 5A, p. 377 / Book 5B, p. 377)

question: Which computer provides the 'A/C ON GROUND' signal to the EIU?
justification: A/C ON GROUND signal from LGCIU. (Shown in block diagrams: Book 5A, p. 142 / Book 5B, p. 229)

question: On the ground with CFM56 engines running, what is the default N1 rate limit displayed, regardless of lever position?
justification: NOTE: On the ground with the engines running the displayed N1 rate limit corresponds to the TO/GA thrust limit whatever the thrust lever position is. (Book 5B, p. 361)

question: Which of the following is a discrete output sent by the EIU for engine operation?
justification: The EIU provides the following discrete outputs... start valve closure. (Book 5B, p. 227)

question: What replaces the white circle 'predicted EPR' on the IAE V2500 ECAM when N1 MODE is selected?
justification: On the N1 indicator, the predicted N1, i.e. the white circle, replaces the predicted EPR. (Book 5A, p. 283)

question: When does the autothrust function become inactive with 2 engines running on a CFM56-5B?

options.a: When levers are set above CLimb

justification: When engaged, the A/THR function becomes inactive when the throttle levers are set above CLimb with 2 engines running. (Book 5B, p. 373)

question: If the EIU receives an 'Engine Fire' command from the fire panel, what is its direct response regarding the LP SOV?

options.a: It signals the ECU to abort combustion
options.b: It outputs 28VDC to both electrical motors of the LP SOV to drive it closed
options.c: It disconnects the IDG to prevent electrical sparks

justification: When the ENGine FIRE P/B is released out, both electrical motors drive the LP SOV to the closed position. (Book 5B, p. 206) [Logic flow through EIU shown in diagrams: Book 5B, p. 207]

question: In what range of TLA can the autothrust function NOT be activated (except in alpha floor) on the CFM56?
justification: In the forward range (35 deg. To 45 deg.TLA), the autothrust function cannot be activated (except in alpha floor condition). (Book 5B, p. 377)

question: How many potentiometers are installed in the IAE V2500 Throttle Control Unit (TCU)?
justification: The throttle control unit comprises: ... -6 potentiometers installed three by three. (Book 5A, p. 379)

question: What abbreviation is used on the ECAM for the Maximum Reverser thrust limit mode on the IAE V2500?
justification: The thrust limit modes are: ... MREV: Maximum Reverser. (Book 5A, p. 267)

question: Which parameter from the engine oil system is sent as a discrete input to the EIU?
justification: The Engine Interface Unit (EIU) receives ... LOP SW. (Block diagram: Book 5B, p. 229)

question: What is the TLA position for the single detent point in the reverse thrust range on the V2500?
justification: In the reverse thrust throttle range, there is one detent point at - 6 deg.TLA. (Book 5A, p. 377)

question: How many ARINC 429 output data buses are received by the IAE V2500 EIU from the EEC?
justification: The EIU receives 2 ARINC 429 output data buses from EEC channels A and B. (Book 5A, p. 140)

question: In the IAE V2500 'Unrated N1 mode', what happens to the engine protection against over-boost (e.g. during Go-Around)?

options.a: It is maintained using EGT limits
options.b: There is no longer an engine protection against over-boost
options.c: The FMGC takes over over-boost protection via the EIU

justification: NOTE: in unrated N1 mode, there is no longer an engine protection against over boost, e.g. Go-Around. (Book 5A, p. 285)

question: On the CFM56-5B, at what N2 percentage is the FADEC logic automatically switched to Control Alternator supply?
justification: Above 58% of N2, the ECU logic automatically switches to the control alternator supply. (Book 5B, p. 230)

question: Which system provides digital inputs to the IAE V2500 EIU for the auto-thrust function?
justification: The Engine Interface Unit (EIU) receives digital inputs from: ... the Flight Control Unit (FCU) for the auto-thrust function. (Book 5A, p. 140)

question: Which air data parameters from the ADR are used by the CFM56-5B ECU to compute the N1 rating limit?

options.c: Air data parameters including TAT, Total Pressure, P0, and Mach

justification: The air data used to validate ... TAT, TOTal PRESSure, P0, mach number. (Book 5A, p. 136 / Book 5B, p. 363)

question: What is the electrical excitation current provided by each IAE V2500 FADEC channel to its dedicated throttle resolver?
justification: Each resolver... receives its electrical excitation current (6 VAC) from the related FADEC channel. (Book 5A, p. 379)

question: Which TLA position corresponds to the 'Reverser Full Throttle stop'?
justification: -20 degrees TLA corresponds to Reverser Full Throttle stop. (Book 5A, p. 377 / Book 5B, p. 377)

question: Which computer sends digital inputs to the IAE V2500 EIU for engine troubleshooting and tests?
justification: The Engine Interface Unit (EIU) receives digital inputs from: - the Centralized Fault Display Interface Unit (CFDIU) for engine troubleshooting and test. (Book 5A, p. 140)

question: On the IAE V2500, what happens to the EPR thrust limit indication if N1 MODE is forced?

options.b: The N1 MODE limit is displayed instead of the EPR limit

justification: On the ECAM... the N1 MODE limit is displayed instead of the EPR limit. (Book 5A, p. 283)

question: What is the N2 threshold for the IAE V2500 EEC to automatically switch from A/C 28V DC to its dedicated alternator supply?
justification: As soon as the engine is running above 10% of N2, the dedicated alternator directly supplies the EEC. (Book 5A, p. 145)

question: To which computer does the IAE V2500 EIU send digital outputs for pneumatic valve operation?
justification: The EIU sends digital outputs to: - the Bleed Monitoring Computer (BMC) for pneumatic valve operation. (Book 5A, p. 140)

question: In the IAE V2500 FADEC system, what is the effect if Mach number input from the ADIRU is invalid but TAT and Pressure remain available?

options.a: EEC reverts to Unrated N1 mode
options.b: EEC uses engine sensors to validate and stays in EPR mode if possible
options.c: EEC reverts to a fixed IDLE setting

justification: The EEC performs validation tests and selection logic... ADIRU data is preferred... The air data used to validate... (Book 5A, p. 136) [Logic indicates it stays in EPR mode using validated air data sources].

question: How does the EIU permit thrust reverser deployment on the CFM56-5B?

options.a: By opening the isolation valve in the HCU
options.b: By energizing the inhibition relay, allowing the directional valve to be opened by the ECU
options.c: By closing the spoiler defense line static relay

justification: Then, the Engine Interface Unit (EIU) permits reverser deployment by energization of the inhibition relay, so the directional valve can be opened by the ECU. (Book 5B, p. 416)

question: Which TLA position on the V2500 corresponds to 'Forward Full Throttle stop'?
justification: +45 degrees TLA corresponds to Forward Full Throttle stop. (Book 5A, p. 377)

question: What happens if the EIU receives an 'A/C on ground' signal from LGCIU and a 'TLA reverse' signal from TCU?

options.b: It energizes the inhibition relay for thrust reverser deployment
options.c: It forces the engine to approach idle

justification: When the aircraft on ground signals from LGCIU and TLA reverse signal from TCU are sent to EIU, the EIU energize the inhibition relay. (Book 5A, p. 331)

question: On an IAE V2500, what occurs if the EIU has failed while the engine is running?

options.b: The continuous relight function is automatically selected by the EEC
options.c: The engine continues in manual mode but cannot be restarted if shut down

justification: Automatic Selection [of Continuous Ignition]: ... EIU HAS FAILED. (Book 5A, p. 176)

question: Where is the N2 speed sensor installed on the IAE V2500 engine?

options.a: On the fan frame strut No. 6
options.b: At the front face of the accessory gearbox

justification: The N2 speed signal is sensed by the dedicated alternator, installed at the front face of the accessory gearbox. (Book 5A, p. 296)

question: How many thermocouple probe assemblies are used to sense and average the EGT on an IAE V2500 engine?
justification: The engine EGT is sensed and averaged by 4 thermocouple probe assemblies are located at station 4.95. (Book 5A, p. 298)

question: On the IAE V2500, at what differential pressure does the scavenge filter switch activate the ECAM CLOG warning?
justification: The ECAM is activated when the differential pressure is greater than 12 PSI. (Book 5A, p. 353/305)

question: On the IAE V2500, when does the oil pressure indication become red on the ECAM?
justification: If the oil pressure gets below 80 PSI the indication becomes amber and red if the pressure drops below 60 PSI. (Book 5A, p. 357)

question: On the IAE V2500, what happens if the oil temperature stays at 157°C for more than 15 minutes?

options.c: An automatic engine shutdown is initiated

justification: Normal temperature is indicated green on ECAM... or steady amber if over temperature condition of 157 °C lasts more than 15 minutes. (Book 5A, p. 357)

question: At which aerodynamic station plane are the IAE V2500 EGT sensors located?
justification: thermocouple probe assemblies are located at station 4.95 (LP turbine exhaust case strut). (Book 5A, p. 298)

question: How is normal vibration processed for display on the ECAM SD?

options.a: As an raw IPS value ranging from 0 to 3.0
options.b: As a ratio of actual value to maximum value, multiplied by 10
options.c: As a percentage of N1 speed

justification: the EVMU processes the ratio actual value/maxi value. This ratio is multiplied by 10 and is available on the EVMU output. (Book 5A, p. 292 / Book 5B, p. 402)

question: On the IAE V2500, what is the maintenance requirement if contamination is found on the Master Magnetic Chip Detector (MCD)?

options.a: Clean the Master MCD and release the aircraft
options.c: Inspect ALL other MCDs on the engine

justification: Note: CONTAMINATION on Master MCD - Inspect ALL other MCD's. (Book 5A, p. 400)

question: Where is the thermocouple junction located for the CFM56-5B EGT measuring plane?

options.a: Between the HPT and the LPT
options.b: In the LPT stage-2 nozzle assembly
options.c: In the turbine rear frame (TRF) struts

justification: thermocouple probes located in the T49.5 plane of Low Pressure Turbine (LPT) stage-2 nozzle assembly. (Book 5B, p. 390)

question: On the CFM56-5B, which sensor is used as a backup for the No. 1 bearing vibration accelerometer?

options.b: The Turbine Rear Frame (TRF) vibration sensor

justification: The TRF vibration sensor is used as back-up of N1 bearing accelerometer to monitor... engine vibration level. (Book 5B, p. 402)

question: On the IAE V2500, where is the Fuel Flow (FF) transmitter mounted?

options.a: On the RH side of the core at 12 o'clock
options.b: On the lower left-hand side of the fan case, rearward of the fuel pump
options.c: Between the FMU and the IDG oil cooler

justification: The fuel flow transmitter... is mounted on the lower left-hand side of the fan case, rearward of the LP/HP fuel pump. (Book 5A, p. 300)

question: Where is the nacelle temperature probe installed on the CFM56-5B?
justification: The nacelle temperature is monitored by a temperature probe installed in the ventilated core compartment. (Book 5B, p. 406)

question: Which of the following indications is ONLY displayed during the engine start sequence on the ECAM?

options.c: Start valve position and Ignition status

justification: * THESE INDICATIONS ARE ONLY DISPLAYED DURING THE START SEQUENCE. (Points to Ignition and Start Valve in diagram: Book 5A, p. 303 / Book 5B, p. 397)

question: At what threshold does the IAE V2500 oil pressure indication turn amber?
justification: If the oil pressure gets below 80 PSI the indication becomes amber. (Book 5A, p. 357)

question: On the IAE V2500, which optional sensor supplies air pressure from the LP compressor exit?
justification: P2.5 sensor supplies air pressure from the LP compressor exit. (Book 5A, p. 314)

question: On the IAE V2500, which component senses oil temperature for the Engine Condition Monitoring (signal to EIU)?

options.a: A dual resistor unit with a sealed wire-wound element
options.b: A single thermocouple on the oil tank
options.c: A probe in the fuel cooled oil cooler header

justification: The oil temperature is sensed by a dual resistor unit. The unit has a sealed, wire-wound resistance element. (Book 5A, p. 305)

question: At what range does the CFM56 oil differential pressure switch generate a main oil filter clog indication?
justification: the ECAM system to generate the main oil filter clog indication when the oil differential pressure... is comprised between 29 psig (2 bar) and 33 psig (2.28 bar). (Book 5B, p. 399)

question: Where is the vibration transducer installed on the IAE V2500 engine case?

options.a: In the fan case at the top left side
options.c: On the front flange of the TRF

justification: Each vibration transducer is installed in the fan case at the top left side of the engine. (Book 5A, p. 308)

question: In the IAE V2500 EGT measuring system, from which direction are the thermocouple probe locations (9.5, 7.5, 4.5, 2 o'clock) viewed?
justification: probe assemblies are located... at 9.5, 7.5, 4.5 and 2 o'clock viewed from the rear. (Book 5A, p. 298)

question: At what oil temperature is a high oil temperature warning triggered on the IAE V2500?
justification: a high oil temperature warning is triggered, if the oil temperature reaches 165 °C. (Book 5A, p. 357)

question: Where is the N1 speed sensor installed on the CFM56-5B?

options.a: In the fan frame strut No. 6 at the 5:00 o'clock position
options.b: On the accessory gearbox rear face

justification: The N1 speed sensor is installed in the fan frame strut No.6 at the 5:00 o'clock position. (Book 5B, p. 388)

question: Which unit computes the 'fuel used' value displayed on the ECAM SD?

options.b: The Full Authority Digital Engine Control (FADEC)

justification: The fuel used value computed by the Full Authority Digital Engine Control (FADEC) is displayed in green on the ECAM SD. (Book 5A, p. 310 / Book 5B, p. 404)

question: Which of the following secondary parameters is NOT permanently displayed on the ECAM ENGINE page?
justification: The engine secondary parameters non permanently displayed on the SD are: ... nacelle temperature indication. (Book 5A, p. 302 / Book 5B, p. 396)

question: On the IAE V2500, what pressure threshold triggers the LOP (Low Oil Pressure) warning?
justification: The Oil LOW PRESSURE switch sends its discrete signal... when the pressure drops below 60 PSI. (Book 5A, p. 357)

question: On the IAE V2500, what provides the high pressure (HP) shaft rotational speed signal to the EEC and ECAM?

options.a: A magnetic pickup in the core
options.b: The dedicated alternator at the front of the accessory gearbox
options.c: A probe assembly at the N°4 bearing

justification: The N2 speed signal is sensed by the dedicated alternator, installed at the front face of the accessory gearbox. (Book 5A, p. 296)

question: On an IAE V2500, if an individual thermocouple probe in an EGT assembly fails, how does the system maintain an average value?

options.a: The EEC automatically reverts to rated N1 mode
options.b: The system averages the remaining valid signals from the 4 assemblies
options.c: The ECAM display turns red and marks 'XX'

justification: The engine EGT is sensed and averaged by 4 thermocouple probe assemblies. (Book 5A, p. 298) [Logic of averaging sensing points implies dismissal of invalid data]

question: On the CFM56-5B, where is the No. 1 bearing vibration sensor (accelerometer) specifically located?

options.b: At 9:00 o'clock position on No. 1 and No. 2 bearing support
options.c: On the accessory gearbox front face

justification: The No. 1 bearing sensor is formed by an accelerometer located at 9:00 o'clock position on No. 1 and No .2 bearing support. (Book 5B, p. 402)

question: On the IAE V2500, where is the scavenge oil temperature thermocouple located?

options.a: In the combined scavenge line between the master magnetic chip detector and the scavenge filter
options.b: Downstream of the pressure pump on the oil tank scupper
options.c: Upstream of the Air Cooled Oil Cooler

justification: The scavenge oil temperature thermocouple is located in the combined scavenge line between the master magnetic chip detector and the scavenge filter. (Book 5A, p. 305)

question: On the IAE V2500, which sensor provides air pressure from the fan exit for condition monitoring through the AIDS?
justification: P12.5 sensor supplies air pressure from the fan exit. (Book 5A, p. 314)

question: Which of the following parameters appears on the ECAM CRUISE page for the IAE V2500?
justification: Fuel used, oil quantity and vibration indications are also displayed on the ECAM CRUISE page. (Book 5A, p. 302)

question: What is the name of the measuring plane for EGT sensors on both A320 engine types?
justification: 9 thermocouple probes located in the T49.5 plane (Book 5B, p. 390) / ...located at station 4.95 (Book 5A, p. 298).

question: A vibration reading of '3' on the engine ECAM indicates what value in Inch Per Second (IPS)?
justification: 1 unit for N1 or N2 rotor corresponds to 0.3IPS. (Book 5A, p. 292 / Book 5B, p. 402) [3 units x 0.3 = 0.9].

question: On the IAE V2500, at what differential pressure does the scavenge filter bypass valve open?
justification: The by-pass valve opens at 20 PSI. (Book 5A, p. 353)

question: To which two units does the CFM56-5B N1 speed sensor directly transmit its signals?
justification: It senses the LP rotor assembly rotational speed and transmits the corresponding signals to the Engine Vibration Monitoring Unit (EVMU) and the ECU. (Book 5B, p. 388)

question: Where is the oil pressure transmitter located on the CFM56-5B?

options.b: On the lubrication unit outlet line
options.c: On the accessory gearbox rear face

justification: The oil pressure XMTR is located on the lubrication unit outlet line. (Book 5B, p. 399)

question: On the IAE V2500, which sensor is specifically used for the 'on-board fan trim balancing' procedure?

options.a: A dual accelerometer on the core

justification: one sensor sends N1 analog signals (trim balance sensor) to the Engine Vibration Monitoring Unit... capable of on-board fan trim balancing. (Book 5A, p. 296/292)

question: At what temperature threshold is the nacelle temperature indication displayed on the IAE V2500 ECAM?
justification: NACELLE TEMPERATURE INDICATION (DISPLAYED IF ONE NACELLE TEMPERATURE IS AT OR ABOVE 320°C). (Book 5A, p. 303)

question: On the IAE V2500, which unit receives the oil temperature analog signal for use in the Heat Management System (HMS)?
justification: Such oil temp analog signal is sent to the related EEC for the Fuel Diverter and Return valve control. (Book 5A, p. 357)

question: What is the specific location of the Tcase sensor on the CFM56-5B?

options.a: At 12 o'clock on the fan frame
options.b: Between the combustion chambers and the HPT

justification: Tcase sensor is located between the combustion chambers and the HPT. (Book 5B, p. 410)

question: On the IAE V2500, how is a transfer to the spare N1 speed sensor performed if the primary sensor fails?

options.a: Automatically in flight by the EEC
options.b: On the ground through the MCDU
options.c: Manually via a toggle switch in the avionics bay

justification: In case of sensor failure, the transfer to the second sensor is carried out on the ground through the MCDU. (Book 5A, p. 292)

question: At what pressure does the IAE V2500 cold start pressure relief valve open?
justification: The cold start pressure relief valve opens at 450 PSI. (Book 5A, p. 350)

question: What is the maximum fuel flow capacity of the transmitter used on the CFM56-5B?
justification: The maximum flow across this XMTR is 6360 kg/hr (14000 lb/hr). (Book 5B, p. 394)

question: Which of the following units does NOT receive a signal from the IAE V2500 N2 indicating system?
justification: The N2 indicating system sends signals... to the EEC... to the ECAM... and to the Engine Vibration Monitoring Unit. (Book 5A, p. 296)

question: On the IAE V2500, what is the measurement range for the oil temperature dual resistor unit?
justification: Temperature measurement range: -60°C to 250°C. (Book 5A, p. 305)

question: On the CFM56-5B, which unit computes the position and amplitude of unbalanced signals from the rotors?
justification: The aircraft EVMU uses the vibration... to extract all the vibration signals and compute the position and the amplitude of the unbalanced signals. (Book 5B, p. 402)

question: Where is the No. 4 bearing pressure transducer installed on the IAE V2500 engine?

options.b: On the right side of the deoiler

justification: The No.4 bearing pressure transducer is installed on the right side of the deoiler. (Book 5A, p. 359)

question: In the IAE V2500, what happens if the SDACs fail while trying to transmit oil quantity data to the DMCs?

options.a: The data is lost and display shows 'XX'
options.b: The EIU sends the data via the FWCs
options.c: The EEC sends the data directly via the high-speed ARINC bus

justification: If there is a failure of the SDACs, the EIU sends data to the DMCs by the FWCs. (Book 5B, p. 222) [Logic applies across single-aisle fleet data architecture].

question: How are the dual accelerometers (A and B) on the IAE V2500 managed during normal operations?

options.a: Both sensors are used and averaged
options.b: Only one sensor is used per flight, automatically selected by the EVMU
options.c: Sensor A is used for N1 and Sensor B for N2

justification: Only one sensor, A or B, of the dual accelerometer is used at a time and during one flight. It is automatically selected by the Engine Vibration Monitoring Unit (EVMU) at each flight. (Book 5A, p. 292)

question: Where is the CFM56-5B oil temperature sensor for Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) cooling system control located?

options.a: On the main oil pressure filter housing

justification: An engine oil temperature sensor for the Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) cooling system control (signal to ECU) is located above the oil tank. (Book 5B, p. 399)

question: On the CFM56-5B, what physical measurement corresponds to 1 unit of vibration on the ECAM?
justification: As normal vibration is depending on rotor speed... This ratio is multiplied by 10... [1 unit corresponds to 0.3IPS per fleet standard]. (Book 5A, p. 292 / Book 5B, p. 402)
